items.title: Transform errors still exit successfully
items.recommendation: When totalErrors is greater than zero, set a non-zero exit code or throw after printing the summary, and avoid printing the success message. If partial writes are expected, make that explicit in the failure message.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature metadata lists no linked tests, and no codemod test/spec files were found for the CLI error path.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a CLI test that forces rewriteImportsInFile to return a result with errors and asserts that anvil-codemod imports exits non-zero and does not print the success message.
items.minimumFixScope: Update the error-summary branch in tools/codemods/src/cli.ts and add focused CLI coverage for transform-error handling.

items.title: CLI version is hard-coded differently from package version
items.recommendation: Read the version from package metadata, inject it at build time, or otherwise keep the Commander version sourced from the same value as tools/codemods/package.json.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature metadata lists no linked tests, and no CLI metadata test was found for --version output.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a CLI metadata test that invokes anvil-codemod --version and compares stdout with tools/codemods/package.json version.
items.minimumFixScope: Update tools/codemods/src/cli.ts version initialisation and add a focused version contract test.

items.title: DiagnosticLocation omits nullable line/column values allowed by the wire contract
items.recommendation: Model the nullable wire form explicitly, e.g. `line?: number | null`, `column?: number | null`, and likely the end span fields if the same null policy applies, or add a parser that normalises null to undefined before exposing `Diagnostic`. Keep the comments, type surface, and tests aligned.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The diagnostics parity test only covers the omitted-property case for path-only locations; it never constructs or parses a diagnostic whose location carries explicit nulls.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a diagnostics wire-parity test for a path-only/deleted-file location with `line: null` and `column: null`, asserting the accepted public representation or the parser normalisation result.
items.minimumFixScope: Update `DiagnosticLocation` and the diagnostics parity tests in `packages/anvil-driver-client/src/diagnostics`.

items.title: Diagnostic category type accepts arbitrary outbound values despite a closed category vocabulary
items.recommendation: Narrow producer-facing `Diagnostic.category` to `Category`, or split the surface into a strict outbound `Diagnostic` and a parsed/inbound diagnostic type that can preserve or normalise unknown category strings.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The diagnostics tests pin known field names and known sample categories, but they do not assert that arbitrary category strings are rejected by the TypeScript contract or normalised on parse.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a type-level contract test for the diagnostics module that rejects `category: 'future-category'` for producer-facing diagnostics, or add a parser test showing unknown categories are converted to `other`.
items.minimumFixScope: Adjust the diagnostics type surface and add a focused diagnostics contract test.

items.title: Admin API key can be exposed through command-line arguments
items.recommendation: Remove the `--key` option from the public CLI surface, or deprecate it in favour of `ANVIL_ADMIN_KEY` plus an interactive secret prompt or protected config source. If compatibility requires keeping it temporarily, emit a warning and document it as unsafe for shared hosts and CI logs.
items.reproduction: Run `anvil-admin --key secret-value list` and inspect the process command line while it is running, or check shell history after invocation; the secret is present as plaintext argv/history.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests exercise error mapping and `--help` exit behaviour; they do not assert secret-handling policy or check that sensitive values avoid argv exposure.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a command-surface test that fails if `buildProgram().helpInformation()` advertises `--key <key>`, and a config-resolution test covering `ANVIL_ADMIN_KEY` as the supported secret path.
items.minimumFixScope: Change the root CLI option registration and the config option contract for admin API key resolution; update tests and user-facing help accordingly.

items.title: In-flight connect can resurrect a closed client and orphan transports
items.recommendation: Serialize connection attempts and invalidate stale completions. Store and return an active connect promise for the connecting state, or track a connection generation token. If close() happens while a connect is pending, ensure the pending transport is closed or ignored when it resolves, and never let openTransport() overwrite closed state. Also clear any scheduled reconnect before an explicit connect path starts a fresh attempt.
items.reproduction: Use a transportFactory whose connect() returns a deferred promise. Call const p = client.connect(), then await client.close() before resolving the deferred. Resolve connect and await p. The client ends in state connected with a live transport even though close() already completed, and request() no longer throws anvil-driver-closed.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing idempotency test only calls connect() after the first connect has fully resolved, so it does not exercise concurrent connect() or close() racing with an unresolved transport.connect().
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test with a deferred fake transport.connect(): start connect(), call close() before resolving the deferred, then resolve it and assert that a subsequent request() rejects with anvil-driver-closed and that the deferred transport's close() was invoked or the transport was not retained. Add a second test for two concurrent connect() calls returning one shared connection attempt.
items.minimumFixScope: DriverClient connection lifecycle state in packages/anvil-driver-client/src/client/driver-client.ts plus focused client tests.

items.title: scan_buffer cannot enforce session ownership because the contract omits sessionId
items.recommendation: Add a sessionId or equivalent authenticated session binding to scan_buffer, validate it against the connection or registered lineage before scanning, and return a structured JSON-RPC error on mismatches.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The only cross-session test is ignored, and the placeholder assertion only checks the generic response envelope rather than requiring rejection. The other linked tests cover JSON-RPC shape, spoofed env-tag handling, and run_foreground wiring, but not session-scoped scan_buffer authorization.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Enable rust_consumer_rejects_cross_session_subscription after extending cross_session_request with a mismatched sessionId, and assert a structured error whose data reason names the session mismatch. Add the same fixture to any consumer contract tests.
items.minimumFixScope: Protocol schema for scan_buffer params, IPC request parsing/validation, registry or connection-session lookup, and the ignored midedit contract test.

items.title: Standalone intercept command lacks executable-level regression coverage
items.recommendation: Add a small executable-level integration test for the anvil-intercept binary, at least covering CLI parsing and malformed .anvil.yaml propagation to a non-zero exit. Keep daemon-liveness behavior in existing run_foreground tests unless a signal-driven binary test can be made reliable.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: daemon_config_wired injects a Resolved config directly into run_foreground, and midedit/jsonrpc tests bind IpcListener directly. None of the linked tests spawn the binary or exercise Cli::parse and config::load_for_daemon_cwd through main.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Create crates/anvil-intercept/tests/standalone_binary.rs using env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_anvil-intercept") or assert_cmd. Run the binary in a temp CWD with malformed .anvil.yaml and assert failure plus the config-load diagnostic; add a --help or missing-subcommand assertion for the Clap surface.
items.minimumFixScope: Integration test only; no production code change is required unless the test exposes a CLI-path defect.

items.title: Malformed JSON-RPC error responses are classified as valid responses
items.recommendation: Make classifyIncoming perform structural validation before returning kind='response': id must be string, number, or null; success responses must have result and no error; error responses must have error as a non-null object with number code and string message, and must not also include result. Return unknown for malformed response envelopes.
items.reproduction: Call classifyIncoming({ jsonrpc: '2.0', id: 'req-1', error: null }); it returns kind='response' even though the value is not a valid JsonRpcErrorResponse. Passing that response to errorFromResponse dereferences null.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The current classifyIncoming tests cover valid success/error responses and a few non-response shapes, but they do not include malformed response-shaped frames with invalid error payloads, invalid ids, or both result and error.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add tests asserting classifyIncoming returns unknown for { jsonrpc: '2.0', id: 'req-1', error: null }, { jsonrpc: '2.0', id: {}, result: true }, and { jsonrpc: '2.0', id: 'req-1', result: true, error: { code: -32603, message: 'x' } }.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil-driver-client/src/framing/jsonrpc.ts plus jsonrpc.test.ts coverage for malformed response-shaped frames.

items.title: Fragmented long lines cause quadratic copying before the size cap trips

evidence.symbol: does not buffer past the cap when newline never arrives

items.recommendation: Store pending data as a list of chunks with a running byte count, and concatenate only once when a complete line is ready to decode. Alternatively use an amortized-growth buffer strategy. Keep the existing maxLineBytes check based on the running byte count so oversize detection still fires before unbounded retention.
items.reproduction: Create a default NdjsonFramer and repeatedly call push(Buffer.from('A')) without a newline until the cap is reached. Each call after the first copies the full accumulated pending buffer, so total copied bytes grow quadratically.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing cap test sends 100 bytes in a single chunk and then another mixed chunk, so it verifies bounded buffering but not fragmented adversarial input or allocation/copy complexity.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that pushes many one-byte or small chunks up to a small maxLineBytes value and asserts only one oversize-line error is emitted; if practical, instrument or expose a chunked implementation invariant so the test prevents per-byte full-buffer copying from returning.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil-driver-client/src/framing/ndjson.ts appendPending/pending representation plus ndjson.test.ts fragmented oversize coverage.

items.title: Expired dedup cache entries are retained for abandoned keys

evidence.symbol: cache expires after the dedup window

items.recommendation: Add bounded eviction: sweep stale entries opportunistically on submit, schedule per-entry expiry, or cap the cache size with LRU semantics. The eviction should remove entries for keys other than the current submit key once they are older than dedupWindowMs.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The cache expiry test only resubmits the same key, which exercises the same-key delete branch. It does not cover stale entries for keys that are never submitted again.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: With a manual scheduler and short dedupWindowMs, submit successful validations for multiple distinct keys, advance past the window, trigger another submit on a different key, and assert stale entries for abandoned keys are evicted via a test-visible cache size or equivalent observable hook.
items.minimumFixScope: MidEditDebouncer dedup cache eviction policy and focused cache-expiry tests

items.title: Pending debounced validations are not cancelled on client close
items.recommendation: Expose a teardown path for the mid-edit validator and have DriverClient.close call it, or pass an abort/lifecycle signal into createMidEditValidator so it can call debouncer.cancelAll immediately on close. The close path should clear pending debounce timers and settle pending validateMidEdit promises deterministically.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing close test advances the scheduler after close and only checks for eventual no-hang, accepting either coalesced or error. It does not assert that close itself clears the debounce timer or settles the promise before the timer fires.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Create a client with a manual midEdit scheduler and debounceMs: 80, call validateMidEdit, close the client without advancing the scheduler, then assert the validation promise settles promptly and sched.pending is 0.
items.minimumFixScope: midedit validator lifecycle plus DriverClient close integration for pending debounced validations

items.title: Unknown diagnostic severities are silently downgraded to informational
items.recommendation: Validate severity at the converter boundary before mapping. For an unknown severity, either throw/return an error observation or fail closed by treating it as blocking and counting it as a violation, whichever matches the Rust authoritative behaviour.
items.reproduction: Call fromMidEditResponse(ctx, { diagnostics: [{ severity: 'critical' as any, source: { rule_id: 'r1' } }] }). The returned observation has enforcement 'informational', no rules_violated, violation_count 0, and warning_count 0.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The severity mapping tests only cover 'error', 'warning', and 'info'. They do not cast or parse a malformed runtime diagnostic, so the fallback path is untested.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test passing a DiagnosticLike with severity: 'critical' as unknown as Severity and assert the chosen fail-closed behaviour, ideally pinned to the Rust mirror.
items.minimumFixScope: Update enforcementFor/countsFor or add a shared severity classifier in packages/anvil-driver-client/src/kindling/types.ts, then extend packages/anvil-driver-client/src/kindling/types.test.ts with the malformed-severity case.

items.title: Pathful admin API base URLs lose their path prefix
items.recommendation: Preserve any base pathname when joining request paths. For example, normalise command paths to relative segments before resolving, or construct the URL by appending path.replace(/^\/+/, '') to a base URL whose pathname is retained.
items.reproduction: Create AdminClient with url 'https://api.example.com/proxy' and call get('/admin/waitlist'); the fetch URL resolves to 'https://api.example.com/admin/waitlist', dropping '/proxy'.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing client tests cover a bare origin and trailing slashes, but they do not cover a base URL with a pathname component.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a client test for url 'https://api.example.com/proxy/' plus get('/admin/waitlist') expecting 'https://api.example.com/proxy/admin/waitlist'.
items.minimumFixScope: AdminClient URL construction and one focused client regression test.

items.title: Vitest is configured to pass when no admin-cli tests are discovered
items.recommendation: Remove passWithNoTests for this package so zero discovered tests fail the package test command.
items.reproduction: Rename or move the admin-cli test files outside the configured include pattern and run the package test script; Vitest is allowed to exit successfully with zero discovered tests.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests validate CLI behavior, not the test-runner failure mode when discovery finds zero files.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/admin-cli/vitest.config.ts only.

items.title: Network requests can hang indefinitely
items.recommendation: Add a request timeout, ideally configurable, using AbortController or AbortSignal.timeout. Map timeout/abort failures to an AdminError with the network-failure exit code and a clear message.
items.reproduction: Use a fetch implementation that returns a never-resolving promise and run any command that calls AdminClient; the command never completes because there is no timeout or abort path.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The client tests cover fetch rejection, 4xx, 5xx, invalid payloads, and validation failures, but not a fetch that never resolves.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a fake-timer test where fetch observes an AbortSignal and never resolves until the timeout aborts, then assert the client rejects with an AdminError exitCode 3.
items.minimumFixScope: AdminClient.request plus one timeout regression test.

items.title: Non-finite reliability options can disable or permanently poison quarantine state
items.recommendation: Validate all numeric options with Number.isFinite before assignment, and require failureThreshold to be a positive safe integer. Consider also requiring windowMs and cooldownMs to be finite integers in milliseconds.
items.reproduction: new ReliabilityBudget({ failureThreshold: Number.NaN }).recordFailure('driver-A') never returns true; new ReliabilityBudget({ failureThreshold: 1, cooldownMs: Number.NaN }).recordFailure('driver-A') followed by isQuarantined('driver-A') returns true indefinitely.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing bad-options test only covers zero and negative values, not NaN, Infinity, or fractional thresholds.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add cases asserting that NaN and Infinity for failureThreshold, windowMs, and cooldownMs throw RangeError; add a fractional failureThreshold case if integer thresholds are required.
items.minimumFixScope: ReliabilityBudget constructor validation plus budget option tests.

items.title: Protocol barrel omits AnvilScanBufferSpoofBlock type
items.recommendation: Add `type AnvilScanBufferSpoofBlock` to the re-export list in `packages/anvil-driver-client/src/protocol/index.ts`.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The protocol tests import directly from `./types.js`, so they validate the type definitions and wire constants but do not exercise the protocol barrel export surface.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a compile-only/export test that imports `type AnvilScanBufferSpoofBlock` from `./index.js` or from the package-level public barrel if that is the actual consumer entrypoint.
items.minimumFixScope: One-line export addition in the protocol barrel plus a focused export-surface test.

items.title: parseAgentTag accepts inherited fields as required wire data
items.recommendation: Require own data properties for the three wire fields before validating their primitive values, for example with Object.hasOwn(obj, 'driver_id') checks or a shared JSON-object helper that rejects inherited required fields.
items.reproduction:
const proto = { driver_id: 'anvil-run', claimed_agent_id: 'forged', pid_starttime: 1 };
parseAgentTag(Object.create(proto)); // currently returns a tag instead of throwing for missing own fields
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The session tests cover null, primitive, array, missing-field, and numeric pid_starttime failures, but they only use ordinary objects with a clean prototype and do not exercise inherited required fields or prototype pollution.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a parseAgentTag test that builds Object.create({ driver_id: 'anvil-run', claimed_agent_id: 'x', pid_starttime: 1 }) and asserts it throws for driver_id, plus a JSON.parse('{"__proto__":{...}}') case if parity with the protection-claim hostile-input tests is desired.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil-driver-client/src/session/types.ts plus packages/anvil-driver-client/src/session/types.test.ts

items.title: Backpressured sends can resolve successfully after the transport closes
items.recommendation: Track pending write waiters as resolve/reject pairs and reject all pending backpressure waiters from fireClose with an anvil-daemon-transport-drop error. Also remove or settle the matching waiter if the write callback reports an error before drain.
items.reproduction: Create a slow-reading Unix socket or named pipe server, call send() with a payload large enough for socket.write() to return false, then close or destroy the server connection before drain fires. The pending send promise resolves via fireClose rather than rejecting with an anvil-daemon-transport-drop error.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included Unix happy-path test sends a small payload and waits for an echo, so socket.write likely returns true and never exercises the queued backpressure path. The Windows tests are pure pipe-name validation and do not exercise send/close behaviour at all.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add transport tests that force socket.write() to return false, close or destroy the peer before drain, and assert the pending send rejects with DriverClientError code anvil-daemon-transport-drop for both Unix and Windows transport implementations or a shared fake socket harness.
items.minimumFixScope: Update the shared send/backpressure bookkeeping in UnixSocketTransport and WindowsNamedPipeTransport, plus targeted regression coverage for pending sends on close/error.

items.title: Absolute request paths discard configured URL path prefixes
items.recommendation: Build request URLs by appending the command path to the configured base pathname instead of passing an absolute-path reference to URL. For example, normalise the base URL once, trim only trailing slashes from its pathname, then append the request path segment while preserving origin and prefix.
items.reproduction: Construct AdminClient with url: 'https://gateway.example.com/anvil' and call get('/admin/waitlist'); the fetch URL becomes 'https://gateway.example.com/admin/waitlist' instead of preserving '/anvil/admin/waitlist'.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The client tests only cover a host-root base URL and trailing slash trimming; they do not exercise a base URL with a non-root pathname.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a client test using url: 'https://api.example.com/prefix/' and get('/admin/waitlist'), expecting 'https://api.example.com/prefix/admin/waitlist'.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/admin-cli/src/client.ts URL construction plus a focused regression in apps/admin-cli/src/__tests__/client.test.ts

items.title: Protection claim parsers accept inherited prototype fields as valid wire data
items.recommendation: Read required fields through an own-property helper, for example Object.hasOwn(obj, key) before accessing obj[key], and treat missing inherited-only fields the same as missing fields. Apply the helper to schema_version, worktree_state, surfaces, identifier, state, and protection_claim envelope extraction if inherited adapter fields should also be rejected.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The hostile-input coverage uses JSON.parse with __proto__, and the test comments explicitly note that JSON.parse does not change the object's prototype. There is no test for Object.create/prototype-polluted objects where normal property lookup resolves required fields from the prototype chain.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add tests that parseProtectionClaim(Object.create({ schema_version: PROTECTION_CLAIM_SCHEMA_VERSION, worktree_state: 'full', surfaces: [] })) throws /schema_version/, and parseSurfaceClaim(Object.create({ identifier: 'mcp', state: 'participating' })) throws /identifier/.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil-driver-client/src/protection_claim/types.ts plus hostile-input regression tests in packages/anvil-driver-client/src/protection_claim/types.test.ts

items.title: Pre-dispatch auth breaks JSON output contracts
items.recommendation: Resolve the effective output mode before the auth gate for commands that expose `--format`, or otherwise detect `--format json` in the raw args for the pre-dispatch branch. Emit informational auth-required JSON envelopes for exit-0 action commands on stdout; reserve stderr for diagnostics and non-zero errors.
items.reproduction: With no credentials, run a gated finding command such as `anvil audit --format json`; the pre-dispatch auth branch runs with `cli.global.json == false`, producing human stderr rather than JSON stdout. With `anvil --json start`, the envelope is emitted to stderr and stdout is empty.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The `--format json` integration test sets `ANVIL_DEV=1`, so it bypasses the pre-dispatch auth branch. The unit tests around `auth_required_response` assert the returned value, but they do not execute the binary or verify stdout versus stderr.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add integration tests that run a gated command without credentials: `audit --format json` should emit a parseable JSON auth-required document on stdout, and `--json start` should not exit 0 with empty stdout.
items.minimumFixScope: Update main.rs pre-dispatch auth output-mode detection and JSON channel routing, plus targeted CLI integration tests for unauthenticated JSON and `--format json` paths.

items.title: Credential load failures are coerced to successful auth-required responses
items.recommendation: Return a distinct non-zero code for credential load failures, such as `EXIT_CONFIG_ERROR` or `EXIT_ERROR`, and only coerce truly expected missing/expired-auth states to success for action commands. If user-facing messaging should remain similar, keep the remediation text but preserve a failing process status for load faults.
items.reproduction: Create an invalid credentials file under the active Anvil config directory, then run a gated action command such as `anvil gate`; `auth::credentials::load()` fails, `evaluate_auth` returns `EXIT_AUTH_REQUIRED`, and `auth_required_response` maps that to `EXIT_OK` for the action command.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Existing unit tests cover `evaluate_auth` and `auth_required_response` separately, but there is no composed integration test with a malformed credentials file asserting that a gated action command exits non-zero.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add an integration test that writes malformed `credentials.json`, runs a gated action command with an isolated config home, and asserts a non-zero exit plus a structured JSON error under `--json`.
items.minimumFixScope: Change the auth evaluation result model in main.rs so credential-load errors are not represented as ordinary auth-required, then add one composed dispatcher-level regression test.

items.title: Rejected DriverClientError does not expose the documented error discriminator
items.recommendation: Add a readonly `error: DriverErrorCode` alias on DriverClientError, initialise it from `payload.error`, and keep `code` as a compatibility alias. Alternatively, if `.code` is the intended direct rejection API, change the DriverError documentation and exported contract so consumers are not told to switch on `.error` for caught request/connect failures.
items.reproduction: Trigger any request rejection, for example a timeout, then inspect the caught value: `err.code` is set but `(err as DriverError).error` is undefined; `err.toJSON().error` is set.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The direct DriverClient tests assert `.code` on rejected values, and the `.error` assertions are on validateMidEdit's result envelope after `DriverClientError.toJSON()`. No test asserts that the caught DriverClientError itself satisfies the exported DriverError shape.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a DriverClient rejection test that catches a timeout or transport-drop error and expects both `err.error` and `err.toJSON().error` to equal the stable discriminator.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil-driver-client/src/errors.ts plus the direct rejection assertions in packages/anvil-driver-client/src/client/driver-client.test.ts

items.title: Kindling parity fixture uses non-canonical Diagnostic fields
items.recommendation: Either make the Kindling fixture a valid Diagnostic using `schema_version` and `summary`, or narrow the helper return type to the actual `DiagnosticLike` contract so the test no longer claims full Diagnostic parity.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The Kindling tests validate only fields derived from severity and source.rule_id; they never serialize or assert the diagnostic object itself against the canonical Diagnostic wire shape.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Update `makeDiag` to build the same canonical fields used by diagnostics/types.test.ts, then add an assertion that the fixture contains `schema_version` and `summary` and does not contain `schema` or `message`.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil-driver-client/src/kindling/types.test.ts

items.title: validateMidEdit silently drops spoof-block scan results
items.recommendation: Model scan_buffer results as a union that includes spoof_block, and map it to a first-class ValidateMidEditResult outcome such as kind:'error' with a stable code or kind:'spoof_block'. Do not cache spoof-block responses as successful diagnostics.
items.reproduction: In packages/anvil-driver-client/src/midedit/validate-mid-edit.test.ts, make the fake daemon respond to validateMidEdit with { jsonrpc:'2.0', id, result:{ version:1, diagnostics:[], truncated:false, spoof_block:{ reason:'degraded:spoofed-attribution', fenced_worktree:'/tmp/wt' } } }. The current switch returns kind:'diagnostics' with an empty diagnostics array instead of a degraded/spoof-block outcome.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The validateMidEdit tests cover forwarding ANVIL_AGENT_TAG and normal daemon errors, but they never simulate a successful JSON-RPC result carrying spoof_block.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a validateMidEdit test where the fake transport returns a scan_buffer result with spoof_block and assert the result is not kind:'diagnostics' or kind:'cached', and that the spoof reason/fenced worktree are preserved.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil-driver-client/src/midedit/validate-mid-edit.ts result types and mapping, plus protocol-aligned tests in validate-mid-edit.test.ts.

items.title: Malformed JSON-RPC error responses can throw instead of becoming structured failures
items.recommendation: Validate response envelopes before classifying them as responses. For error responses, require error to be a non-null object with a finite numeric code and string message; otherwise emit a framing_error/error event and reject the matching pending request with a structured non-retriable daemon/protocol error.
items.reproduction: With a connected DriverClient and an in-flight request id req-1, push the inbound line {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":"req-1","error":null}\n through the fake transport. The framer parses JSON successfully, classifyIncoming marks it as a response, and errorFromResponse throws while reading response.error.message.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: jsonrpc.test.ts covers valid success/error responses and unknown non-response shapes, but it does not cover malformed response envelopes with an id plus invalid result/error payloads.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add tests for classifyIncoming/DriverClient where error is null, error.code is missing, or result and error are both present; assert no synchronous throw and a structured failure or framing_error is produced.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil-driver-client/src/framing/jsonrpc.ts validation and DriverClient.handleResponse error handling, with JSON-RPC malformed-response tests.

items.title: Free-text user fields can inject control sequences into text-mode show output
items.recommendation: Expose a shared text sanitiser from format.ts and apply it to all non-JSON human output that interpolates user/API text, at minimum renderUserPanel fields and other direct status/banner interpolations that include email/name/notes-like values.
items.reproduction: Create or mock a show response with user.name set to "Mallory\nstatus: active" or user.notes containing "\u001b[2J" and run runShowCommand in text mode; stdout includes the injected line/control sequence verbatim.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included sanitisation test covers renderTable only. The included command tests exercise safe sample strings and do not cover control characters in show user fields or other direct text-mode interpolations.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a runShowCommand text-mode test with user.name and user.notes containing newlines, tabs, and ANSI escape bytes, asserting the emitted USER panel remains single-line per field and contains no raw control characters.
items.minimumFixScope: Add one reusable sanitiseText/displayText helper in apps/admin-cli/src/format.ts and use it in apps/admin-cli/src/commands/show.ts for user.email, user.name, user.status, user.id, and user.notes; then extend to invite/revoke direct human messages if the helper is intended to cover all CLI text output.

items.title: Root TypeScript include list is partially dead and does not check eslint.config.mjs
items.recommendation: Either remove the stale/uncheckable include entries, or make the intended files actually checked by moving ESLint config to a TypeScript config file or enabling JS checking intentionally, and update the e2e glob to the real location if root-level checking is intended.
items.reproduction: Run `pnpm exec tsc -p tsconfig.json --showConfig` and inspect `files`: only `./vitest.config.ts` and `./playwright.config.ts` are present despite the broader include list.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests exercise the effective root TypeScript file set or assert that the include list matches existing, checked files.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a small config validation script/test that runs `tsc --showConfig` for the root tsconfig and asserts that every include entry is either intentionally unmatched/ignored with a documented reason or appears in the effective file set/project references.
items.minimumFixScope: tsconfig.json include list, plus any corresponding config-file rename or compiler option change if eslint.config.mjs is intended to be checked.

items.title: Root Vitest discovery omits several in-repo test suites
items.recommendation: Either make the root Vitest include patterns cover every intended non-e2e suite, or replace the root config with an explicit Vitest workspace/project setup that delegates to each package/app config. If this file is not intended as a repository-level runner, remove the misleading broad include comment and avoid passWithNoTests at the root so misuse fails visibly.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No meta-test or validation checks that the root Vitest config discovers all checked-in non-e2e test files.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a small config validation test or script that enumerates non-e2e test files and asserts each one is matched by the root Vitest include/exclude policy, with explicit allow-listing for suites that are intentionally run elsewhere.
items.minimumFixScope: Update vitest.config.ts discovery policy and add a lightweight discovery coverage check.

items.title: Duplicate override authorities have drifted apart
items.recommendation: Keep a single authoritative override block for the package manager actually used by the repository, or add a generated/validated mirror with a manifest drift check that fails when the two blocks diverge unintentionally.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked manifest-drift test is included for this feature, and package.json itself has no validation script that asserts the two override blocks are intentionally equivalent or intentionally different.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a manifest validation test that parses package.json and either rejects top-level `overrides` in this pnpm workspace or verifies it is generated from `pnpm.overrides` according to documented rules.
items.minimumFixScope: package.json override configuration and, if keeping both blocks, the repository's manifest validation test suite.

items.title: Root E2E script bypasses the maintained E2E harness
items.recommendation: Change `test:e2e` to delegate to the maintained harness, for example `pnpm --filter @eddacraft/anvil-e2e test`, or rename the Playwright command to an explicit legacy/playwright-specific script if it is still intentionally supported.
items.reproduction: From the repository root, compare `pnpm test:e2e` with `pnpm test:e2e:harness`; the former invokes Playwright directly while the latter invokes the workspace E2E harness.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked package-script contract test is included for this feature, and the existing script list allows both the stale root command and the maintained harness commands to coexist without asserting they target the same E2E surface.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a package-script contract test that parses package.json and asserts `test:e2e` delegates to the canonical `@eddacraft/anvil-e2e` harness command.
items.minimumFixScope: package.json scripts only, plus a package-script contract test if the repository has an existing manifest validation suite.

items.title: BMAD conversion records invalid-path errors but still returns a successful plan
items.recommendation: Change BMAD conversion so path-conversion errors are surfaced. The narrow fix is to throw when errors.length > 0 so BMADFormatAdapter.parse returns createParseError. A richer fix is to return a conversion object containing plan, errors, and warnings, and have BMADFormatAdapter.parse fail on errors while preserving warnings.
items.reproduction: Parse a structured BMAD agent YAML whose metadata.id or menu exec path is ../../outside.md. safePath rejects it, bmadToAPS records INVALID_PATH, then parse still returns success with the invalid change omitted and no errors exposed.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The edge-case test only verifies that a malformed requirement ID does not produce a dangerous path and explicitly expects parse success. It does not cover structured YAML path fields or assert that accumulated INVALID_PATH errors reach ParseResult.errors.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add BMAD agent/workflow/module YAML fixtures with traversal paths in metadata.id, menu exec/workflow, instructions, validation, and directories, and assert adapter.parse returns success false with INVALID_PATH rather than silently omitting changes.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/adapters/src/bmad/parser.ts conversion result/error handling plus BMADFormatAdapter.parse propagation and targeted BMAD path-error tests.

items.title: APS index files are detected but parsed through the leaf-task path
items.recommendation: Either make APSMarkdownAdapter.parse reject index files with a structured unsupported-format error, or route Modules documents through an index parser and preserve module paths/dependencies in the returned representation. Detection should not claim support for a document shape that parse cannot faithfully convert.
items.reproduction: Pass an APS index containing only ## Modules and .aps.md Path entries to registry.detectAdapter, then call parse on the returned adapter; the detected index content has no task-derived proposed changes.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included APS adapter tests assert index detection and confidence, but the parse tests only use leaf specs with Tasks and never parse a Modules-only index file.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add an APSMarkdownAdapter test that parses a Modules index fixture and asserts either a clear parse failure for unsupported index conversion or a faithful representation of module links and dependencies.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/adapters/src/aps-markdown/adapter.ts detection/parse branching and APS markdown adapter tests for Modules index parse behavior.

items.title: Configured dist publish produces an unresolvable package and hides documented subpaths
items.recommendation: Make the release layout self-consistent. Either publish from the project root with dist files included, or generate/copy a dist/package.json whose main, types, and exports are relative to dist, such as ./index.js and ./index.d.ts. Add explicit exports for the documented subpaths or update the README to only document root imports that actually exist.
items.reproduction: Build and publish/pack from the configured packageRoot, then try importing @eddacraft/anvil-adapters and @eddacraft/anvil-adapters/bmad from the packed artifact.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included Vitest suites import source files such as ../bmad/format-adapter.js and exercise adapter behavior directly; they do not build, pack, or import the configured package artifact through Node package resolution.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a package smoke test that runs the adapters build, packs or stages the configured publish root, and imports the root plus each documented subpath from a temporary consumer project.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/adapters/package.json exports and entrypoints, packages/adapters/project.json publish root or build packaging step, and README examples if the intended public API changes.

items.title: domainImports accepts import IDs for the wrong domain
items.recommendation: Parse the import ID into project/team parts and the trailing domain, then require that trailing domain to exactly equal the domainImports key. Keep the existing key-in-domains and project ID validation.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The tests cover keys not present in domains, malformed import IDs, normal project IDs, and team-prefixed IDs, but they do not cover a syntactically valid import ID whose trailing domain differs from the domainImports key.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a domainImports test that constructs VercelApp with domains: ['example.com'] and domainImports: { 'example.com': 'prj_test123abc/other.com' }, then expects construction to throw with a domain mismatch error.
items.minimumFixScope: Update VercelApp domainImports validation and add one focused unit test in infra/src/__tests__/vercel-app.test.ts.

items.title: Crate docs still say adversarial refresh detection is out of scope while the API exports it
items.recommendation: Update the crate-level docs to move adversarial-refresh detection out of the deferred list and describe the exported `analyze_refresh`/`RefreshSuspicion` API and its tuning caveats, or remove the re-exports if the API is not intended to be public yet.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: This is documentation/API-surface drift; runtime tests for the analyzer would not fail when the crate-level scope prose is stale.
items.minimumFixScope: Edit `crates/anvil-baseline/src/lib.rs` crate docs so the documented scope matches the public re-export list.

items.title: SpecKit v2 derives write paths from unsanitized scenario titles
items.recommendation: Generate path-safe slugs from scenario titles and pass every derived path through validateRelativePath before constructing a Change. Return a conversion error or warning if a safe path cannot be produced.
items.reproduction: Convert a v2 spec whose user scenario heading is `### P1: ../../.github/workflows/pwn`; the resulting APS change path is derived directly from that title instead of being rejected or safely slugged.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included linked test only covers the generic parser input-size guard and does not exercise SpecKit v2 scenario-to-change path derivation.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a SpecKitImportAdapterV2 conversion test with a traversal-like scenario title and assert conversion fails or produces a normalized relative path that cannot escape the repo.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/adapters/src/speckit/import-v2.ts path derivation and tests for v2 import conversion.

items.title: SpecKit parser size guard counts UTF-16 code units instead of bytes
items.recommendation: Use Buffer.byteLength(content, 'utf8') or a shared byte-length guard before parsing SpecKit markdown.
items.reproduction: Pass parseSpecMarkdown a string of repeated 4-byte emoji whose content.length is <= 2 * 1024 * 1024 but Buffer.byteLength(content, 'utf8') is greater; the current guard does not throw.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included size-guard tests are only for parseGeneric; there is no corresponding SpecKitParser multi-byte boundary test.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Mirror the generic parser multi-byte size test for SpecKitParser.parseSpecMarkdown.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/adapters/src/speckit/parser.ts size check and a focused SpecKit parser test.

items.title: Official SpecKit v2 adapter is not exported from the package entrypoint
items.recommendation: Export SpecKitImportAdapterV2 from packages/adapters/src/speckit/index.ts and ensure the package root entrypoint re-exports the speckit barrel if that is the established package pattern.
items.reproduction: A consumer importing from @eddacraft/anvil-adapters can only reach symbols re-exported through dist/index.js; SpecKitImportAdapterV2 is absent from the included speckit barrel and deep package subpaths are not exported.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included linked test does not compile against the package public entrypoint or assert exported adapter symbols.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add an API surface test that imports SpecKitImportAdapterV2 from the package entrypoint used by consumers.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/adapters/src/speckit/index.ts plus any root adapter barrel that feeds dist/index.js.

items.title: Exporting an empty plan emits NaN progress
items.recommendation: Handle the zero-task case explicitly, for example progress 0% with total/completed/remaining all zero, or make empty changes invalid for export if tasks.md requires at least one task.
items.reproduction: Call SpecKitExportAdapter.convertFromAPS with a valid APSPlan whose proposed_changes is []; the tasksContent progress line becomes `- Progress: NaN%`.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included linked test covers generic parser size limits and does not exercise SpecKit export progress generation.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a SpecKitExportAdapter test for an APS plan with no proposed_changes and assert tasksContent does not contain NaN.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/adapters/src/speckit/export.ts generateTasksMarkdown zero-task handling.

items.title: SpecKit imports create non-unique placeholder APS identities
items.recommendation: Use the existing deterministic plan id helper where content is available, or include enough entropy/content hash for generated plans. Compute generateHash on the final APSPlan instead of leaving placeholder hashes.
items.reproduction: Call SpecKitImportAdapterV2.generateSpec or convertToAPS twice within the same truncated timestamp window; both plans can share the same aps-* id and both carry an all-zero hash.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included linked test is for packages/adapters/src/generic and does not assert SpecKit plan id uniqueness or hash validity.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add tests that import/generate two SpecKit plans in quick succession and assert ids are distinct or deterministic by content as intended, and that hash is not the all-zero placeholder and matches generateHash on the returned plan shape.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/adapters/src/speckit/import.ts and packages/adapters/src/speckit/import-v2.ts id/hash creation paths.

items.title: Prebuilt Ember mocks age into expired active data
items.recommendation: Build scenario timestamps relative to now, or inject a clock/currentTime into the mock so prebuilt active fixtures remain active deterministically in tests.
items.reproduction: Call mockEmberWithProposals().getActiveProposals() on any date after February 2024; it returns an empty array even though the fixture initialises three proposals with status 'active'.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included provenance-chain tests create their own mock ports and do not exercise mockEmberWithProposals, mockEmberWithMixedStatuses, or getActiveProposals.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Assert mockEmberWithProposals().getActiveProposals() returns the expected active proposal count under a controlled clock.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/edda-stack/src/testing/mocks/ember.mock.ts and focused mock tests.

items.title: Mock supersede creates invalid evolution state
items.recommendation: Have supersedeMemoryImpl fetch and validate the old memory before creating the replacement, reject or throw when it is missing/non-active, and mark the old memory as 'superseded' with superseded_by when the operation succeeds.
items.reproduction: Call createMockEddaPort().supersedeMemory(nonexistentId, validInput). The mock stores a new memory, retireMemoryImpl returns null, and the result contains old: null even though the API type says MemoryObject.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included test file covers provenance validators only and has no tests for Edda mock supersession behaviour or missing old-memory handling.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add mock tests for successful supersede status/link updates and for missing oldMemoryId leaving the store unchanged while rejecting or returning a documented failure.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/edda-stack/src/testing/mocks/edda.mock.ts and focused mock tests.

items.title: Testing entrypoint is blocked by package exports
items.recommendation: Add './testing' and, if deep testing imports are supported, './testing/*' entries pointing to dist/testing/index.js and dist/testing/*.js with matching type declarations.
items.reproduction: After packaging/building, import '@eddacraft/anvil-edda-stack/testing' from another package. Node/TypeScript package resolution will reject the subpath because it is absent from package.json exports.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests import testing helpers by relative source paths, so they do not exercise the installed package subpath contract.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a package export smoke test or typecheck fixture that imports createMockKindlingPort from '@eddacraft/anvil-edda-stack/testing'.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/edda-stack/package.json, plus a small package-resolution smoke test if this package has export tests.

items.title: Provenance validator accepts mismatched referenced metadata
items.recommendation: Fetch the referenced observation/proposal with getObservation/getProposal during validation and compare stored session_id, kind, timestamp, proposal type, confidence, and created_at against the ref. Use stored timestamps for temporal checks or report mismatches before temporal validation.
items.reproduction: Create a stored observation with session A and timestamp T1, then validate a KindlingRef with the same observation_id but session B and timestamp T2 plus source_sessions [B]. The current code only calls observationExists and then validates B against [B], so it does not detect the mismatch.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included validator tests cover matching refs and missing IDs, but do not include cases where the ID exists and the rest of the reference metadata is wrong.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add tests where a KindlingRef reuses an existing observation_id with a different session_id/timestamp and where an EmberRef reuses an existing proposal_id with a different proposal_type/created_at; expect validation issues.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/edda-stack/src/testing/validators/provenance-chain.ts and its associated test file.

items.title: CWD restoration is treated as file-wide rather than after the final chdir
items.recommendation: Track chdir operations in order and require a saved-cwd restoration after the last non-restoration chdir, or scope the analysis to hooks/tests so each mutation path has a following restoration.
items.reproduction: const originalCwd = process.cwd(); process.chdir(originalCwd); process.chdir('/tmp/test'); is accepted because hasCwdRestoration was set before the leaking chdir.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The tests cover multiple chdirs followed by restoration, but not a restoration that appears before a later cwd-changing call.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add an invalid case with const originalCwd = process.cwd(); process.chdir(originalCwd); process.chdir('/tmp/test');.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/eslint-plugin-anvil/src/rules/require-cwd-restoration.ts and its rule tests

items.title: Published plugin metadata reports a stale version
items.recommendation: Keep plugin.meta.version in sync with package.json, preferably by generating it from the package version during build or by adding a test that asserts the two values match.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included RuleTester suites exercise individual rules only; they do not import the plugin entrypoint or compare metadata to the package manifest.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add an entrypoint test that imports the plugin and package.json and expects plugin.meta.version to equal packageJson.version.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/eslint-plugin-anvil/src/index.ts plus an entrypoint metadata test

items.title: Mock cleanup detection accepts comments or strings as real cleanup
items.recommendation: Inspect the afterEach callback AST for a CallExpression whose callee is vi.restoreAllMocks, instead of matching raw source text.
items.reproduction: A file with vi.spyOn(console, 'log') and afterEach(() => { /* vi.restoreAllMocks() */ }) will be treated as valid.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing invalid tests cover an afterEach with vi.clearAllMocks(), but not a comment, string literal, or nested non-executed occurrence of vi.restoreAllMocks().
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add invalid RuleTester cases where afterEach contains only a comment and only a string literal mentioning vi.restoreAllMocks().
items.minimumFixScope: packages/eslint-plugin-anvil/src/rules/require-mock-cleanup.ts and its rule tests

items.title: Prototype rule IDs are treated as architecture rules
items.recommendation: Use own-property checks for ARCH_RULES, for example Object.hasOwn(ARCH_RULES, ruleId), or define ARCH_RULES with a null prototype/Map and reuse the same own-key predicate in createBoundaryExplanation, getBoundaryExplanation, and isArchitectureRule.
items.reproduction: Call isArchitectureRule('constructor') and it returns true. Call getBoundaryExplanation('__proto__', { file: 'x.ts', line: 1 }) and it does not return null even though no such rule is registered.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing tests assert that 'UNKNOWN-001' is rejected, but they do not include inherited Object.prototype property names, which are the values that bypass the current checks.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add boundary-explainer tests asserting isArchitectureRule('constructor'), isArchitectureRule('toString'), and getBoundaryExplanation('__proto__', mockContext) all reject the rule as unknown/null.
items.minimumFixScope: Update boundary-explainer rule membership checks to require own keys and add regression coverage for prototype-property rule IDs.

items.title: Entrypoint route composition is mostly untested by linked route suites
items.recommendation: Add a small entrypoint-level test suite that imports apps/anvil-api/src/index.ts with DB/key dependencies mocked and exercises representative production paths under /api/v1, including one auth route, one admin route, /health, and one middleware-observable behavior such as CORS or rate-limit headers.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked tests validate route modules directly at /auth, /auth/session, /auth/otp, /auth/github, /auth/device, and /admin. They do not exercise the exported app from index.ts or its /api/v1 base path and global middleware stack.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Import ../index.js in an entrypoint test with mocked getClient and licence probes, then assert requests such as /api/v1/auth/verify and /api/v1/admin/audit reach the intended routers while /auth/verify does not, and assert /api/v1/health returns the expected ok/degraded shape.
items.minimumFixScope: Test-only change covering apps/anvil-api/src/index.ts composition.

items.title: Expired and stale lock takeover can produce split-brain ownership
items.recommendation: Serialise all lock state transitions for a resource with the same exclusive sentinel, or implement compare-and-swap style writes/deletes that verify the observed lock identity immediately before replacing or unlinking it. Apply this to forceAcquire, renewLock, release, and cleanupExpiredLocks, not just createLock.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The lock tests cover contention, release, and a single expired-lock takeover, but they do not run two takeover attempts concurrently and do not exercise an expired owner releasing while another agent acquires.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Create an expired lock, start two LockManager instances with different agents, race their acquire({ type: 'action', resource: 'gate' }) calls, and assert exactly one returns acquired=true. Add a second test where the expired original owner calls release while another agent force-acquires and assert the new lock remains present.
items.minimumFixScope: LockManager lock-file mutation paths for takeover, renewal, release, and cleanup.

items.title: Agent registry updates can overwrite other agents' registrations and heartbeats
items.recommendation: Protect registry mutations with a registry-level file lock, or store one file per agent to avoid whole-registry read-modify-write conflicts. Keep reads lock-free if needed, but every write path should serialise and reload inside the critical section before saving.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No included concurrency test imports AgentManager or exercises concurrent register/heartbeat/cleanup behaviour.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Run two AgentManager instances with different agent IDs against the same workspace, call register concurrently many times, then assert the registry contains both agents and that heartbeat counts are not lost across concurrent heartbeat calls.
items.minimumFixScope: AgentManager write paths and an atomic registry mutation helper.

items.title: Fair queue can be bypassed and queue entries can be lost under concurrent mutation
items.recommendation: Use the same queue lock around every read-modify-write or delete of a queue file. In waitForLock, inspect the queue first and skip the direct acquisition fast path when there are existing queued entries not belonging to this agent.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The queue tests cover basic join, leave, getStatus, and priority sorting, but there are no waitForLock tests and no tests that run join/leave/cleanup concurrently across QueueManager instances.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test with one held lock and two queued agents, release the holder, then start a third agent's waitForLock and assert the queued first agent acquires before the newcomer. Add a concurrent join/leave test that asserts no agent entries are dropped.
items.minimumFixScope: QueueManager waitForLock, leave, getStatus cleanup path, cleanupAllTimedOut, and any helper needed to share queue-file locking.

items.title: Generated git hook imports an unexported concurrency subpath
items.recommendation: Either add './concurrency' to package.json exports with dist/concurrency/index.js and types, or change getHookSetupCommand to import the root package export that already re-exports the concurrency API. Avoid swallowing the setup failure silently in the generated hook.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: git-agent tests validate trailer parsing, command argument safety, and formatting, but they do not assert that getHookSetupCommand references an exported package subpath or execute the generated hook against the package exports map.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a package manifest test that asserts every package subpath used by getHookSetupCommand is present in package.json exports, or execute the generated import string against the built package and fail on ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/runtime/package.json exports and/or getHookSetupCommand.

items.title: Non-ASCII or punctuation-only items collapse to the same generated path
items.recommendation: Generate a fallback slug when sanitisation yields an empty string, and consider using a Unicode-aware slugifier or appending a deterministic short hash to avoid collisions after truncation/sanitisation.
items.reproduction: Parse a document with `## Requirements` containing `- 支払いを追加` and `- ログインを追加`; both generated changes use the same empty-slug path under src/features/.ts even though the descriptions differ.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The parser tests only exercise the size guard and do not assert generated changes or paths for parsed requirements, tasks, or features.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add parser tests for non-ASCII requirement items and for two items that sanitise to the same slug, asserting generated paths are non-empty, valid relative paths, and unique.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/adapters/src/generic/parser.ts itemToChange path generation and parser tests for generated change paths.

items.title: Adapter hashes parsed plans using the placeholder hash field
items.recommendation: Compute the hash from a copy with the hash field omitted, or build the plan without hash first and add hash only after hashing the hashless payload. Keep parseGeneric/genericToAPS internal placeholder handling from leaking into the final hash calculation.
items.reproduction: Parse any generic markdown through GenericMarkdownAdapter.parse, then recompute the hash over the returned plan with the hash field removed; it will not match the returned hash because the adapter hashed the placeholder-bearing object.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included parser tests only cover the input size guard, and the serializer tests never exercise GenericMarkdownAdapter.parse or validate returned plan hashes.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a GenericMarkdownAdapter.parse test that parses a minimal planning document, removes hash from the returned plan, recomputes generateHash on the hashless object, and expects it to equal result.plan.hash.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/adapters/src/generic/format-adapter.ts hash calculation, with a focused adapter parse regression test.

items.title: Validation can accept content that parseGeneric always rejects
items.recommendation: Apply the same MAX_INPUT_SIZE byte-length guard in validate, preferably by sharing a helper or exported constant with parseGeneric so the limits cannot drift.
items.reproduction: Create content larger than 2 MiB containing a markdown heading, a Requirements section, and enough bullet items to exceed the fallback confidence threshold. GenericMarkdownAdapter.validate(content) can return valid, but GenericMarkdownAdapter.parse(content) returns a PARSE_ERROR from parseGeneric's size guard.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The parser tests verify parseGeneric rejects oversized ASCII and multi-byte content, but there is no GenericMarkdownAdapter.validate test for oversized content or validate/parse consistency.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a validate test for oversized planning-looking markdown and assert valid is false with an input-size error; also add a paired test that validate and parse agree on rejecting the same oversized multi-byte content.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/adapters/src/generic/format-adapter.ts validation logic plus focused validation tests.

items.title: README says traversal attempts throw, but exists intentionally returns false
items.recommendation: Update the README/API notes to state that read, readBuffer, write, delete, list, and mkdir throw on traversal, while exists returns false without touching the escaped path.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included test covers and codifies the exists behaviour, but there is no documentation consistency check that would catch the README overstatement.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a README/API contract test or documentation lint assertion only if this repository already has a pattern for doc-code contract checks; otherwise a docs-only fix is sufficient.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/shared/storage/README.md

items.title: Path sandboxing is vulnerable to symlink time-of-check/time-of-use races
items.recommendation: Make the sandbox guarantee atomic with the operation or narrow the documented contract. For writes and mkdir, avoid using a separately validated path string across an await boundary; walk path components with lstat checks, reject symlinks in parents, use no-follow/open-style safeguards where available, and revalidate the parent immediately before committing the write. If adversarial concurrent mutation is out of scope, document that baseDir must not be writable by untrusted concurrent actors.
items.reproduction: Create base/race as a real directory and an outside directory. Loop storage.write('race/target.txt', 'pwn') while another process repeatedly removes base/race and recreates it as a symlink to the outside directory between validation and write. A successful race writes outside/target.txt.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The tests construct symlinks before invoking storage methods and assert rejection. They do not attempt to mutate the checked path after resolvePath succeeds and before the filesystem operation follows the path.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a deterministic test hook or injectable filesystem adapter that pauses after resolvePath validation, swaps a checked parent directory for an external symlink, then resumes write/list/read and asserts the operation is rejected and the outside directory is unchanged.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/shared/storage/src/file-storage.ts path resolution and filesystem operation sequencing, plus symlink race regression coverage.

items.title: downloadBundle returns tampered cache-entry paths on cache hits
items.recommendation: Apply the same `isWithinCacheDir(entry.path)` check before every return of `existingEntry.path` in `downloadBundle()`. If it fails, delete or ignore the entry and force a safe re-download.
items.reproduction: Create `cacheDir/safe-name`, poison `cacheDir/index.json` with `entries.safe-name.path` set to an outside directory and `expires_at` in the future, construct BundleManager with that cacheDir and add bundle `safe-name`, then call `downloadBundle('safe-name')`; it returns success with the outside path.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The regression test covers `getBundle()` rejecting a poisoned path, but it does not call `downloadBundle()` with a valid unexpired poisoned entry or a 304 path.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Extend `bundle-manager.name-escape.test.ts` with a poisoned index, an existing `cacheDir/safe-name`, and a future `expires_at`, then assert `downloadBundle('safe-name')` does not return the outside path.
items.minimumFixScope: BundleManager cache-hit and 304-not-modified return paths.

items.title: Advertised Ed25519 signature verification always fails on Node crypto
items.recommendation: Use Node's one-shot Ed25519 verification API with a Buffer payload, or remove Ed25519 from the exported/default supported algorithms until implemented. Add a generated Ed25519 keypair test with a valid signed manifest.
items.reproduction: In Node, `require('crypto').createVerify('ed25519')` throws `Invalid digest`; the BundleVerifier Ed25519 branch uses that exact call before verification.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked BundleVerifier tests exercise RSA, EC, env, file, and unsigned-file cases, and `rg` finds no Ed25519 test coverage.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Generate an Ed25519 key pair in `bundle-verifier.test.ts`, sign the canonical files array with `crypto.sign(null, Buffer.from(data), privateKey)`, and assert `verifyBundle()` succeeds for an Ed25519 manifest.
items.minimumFixScope: BundleVerifier Ed25519 branch and corresponding algorithm tests.

items.title: OPA binary downloader has unbounded recursive redirect handling
items.recommendation: Add a `redirectsRemaining` parameter and timeout handling to OPABinaryManager.downloadFile, mirroring the BundleManager redirect guard, and clean up the destination file on all rejection paths.
items.reproduction: Point the downloader at an HTTPS endpoint that 302 redirects to itself; `downloadFile()` recurses with no decreasing limit.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The OPABinaryManager tests verify URL shape and mock `downloadBinary()` for forceDownload; they do not exercise redirect loops or timeout behaviour.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Mock `downloadFile()` through a local HTTPS redirect loop or factor redirect handling for injection, then assert the download rejects with `Too many redirects` and removes the partial file.
items.minimumFixScope: OPABinaryManager.downloadFile redirect and timeout handling.

items.title: Unvalidated OPA version can escape the binary cache path
items.recommendation: Validate `version` at construction with a strict version pattern such as `/^\d+\.\d+\.\d+$/`, reject separators and NULs, and assert the resolved binary path remains inside `cacheDir` before any exists/unlink/write/chmod/exec operation.
items.reproduction: Set `ANVIL_OPA_VERSION=1.16.1/../../victim`, choose a cacheDir under a temp directory, create the resolved victim file name outside the cache, then call `ensureBinary()` or `forceDownload()`; the code reaches `unlinkSync(binaryPath)` on the escaped path.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The version tests only use normal dotted versions and assert message propagation; they do not cover separator-bearing or traversal-shaped versions.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add an OPABinaryManager test that sets `ANVIL_OPA_VERSION` or `config.version` to a value containing `/../`, asserts construction or `ensureBinary()` rejects, and verifies a sentinel outside `cacheDir` is not deleted.
items.minimumFixScope: OPABinaryManager version validation plus a cache-path containment guard around `getBinaryPath()` consumers.

items.title: signature_key bundle downloads cannot succeed because no signature sidecar is fetched or path-resolved
items.recommendation: Define the signature contract explicitly: either add a signature URL/sidecar download path and read key files when paths are supplied, or remove/deprecate `signature_key` from BundleManager in favour of BundleVerifier's `.signatures.json` verification. Add tests for both inline PEM and key-file cases if retained.
items.reproduction: Configure a bundle with a valid URL and `signature_key` while leaving `verifySignatures` at its default `true`; after the tarball download, `${tempFile}.sig` is absent and `downloadBundle()` returns `Signature verification failed`.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The BundleManager test fixture disables signature verification in setup and there is no linked test exercising `signature_key` with `verifySignatures: true`.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a BundleManager test that serves a tarball and matching signature sidecar, supplies an inline public key and then a key-file path, and expects a successful verified download; also assert missing signature sidecar produces a clear error.
items.minimumFixScope: BundleManager signature verification configuration and tests.

items.title: Emitter helpers can return link IDs for observations that were dropped
items.recommendation: Preserve non-blocking defaults if required, but expose an awaitable result or failure hook for callers that need reliable governance linkage. At minimum, document that returned IDs are generated-only and add debug/error reporting for dropped observations.
items.reproduction: Use a stub service whose emit method returns Promise.reject(new Error('store down')), then call emitActionExecuted. The function returns an action ID and the rejection is swallowed, leaving no persisted action for that ID.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked emitter tests were provided, and existing inspected tests exercise KindlingService behavior directly rather than rejected service.emit paths through these helper APIs.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add tests for one generated-ID emitter and one provided-ID emitter using a rejecting service; assert the chosen API either surfaces the failure through an awaitable path or explicitly documents/records the drop.
items.minimumFixScope: Apply a shared emission helper or consistent async/error-reporting contract across all emitter files so every public helper has the same reliability semantics.

items.title: Human input emitter returns an ID that is never emitted
items.recommendation: Either add an input_id field to the human_input observation contract and populate it here, or stop generating/returning an ID and change the public return contract to the actual linkable value such as session_id plus timestamp/target.
items.reproduction: Call emitHumanInput with a spy service that records the emitted observation. The returned string is a UUID, but JSON.stringify(recordedObservation) does not contain that UUID.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature metadata lists no linked tests, and the inspected package tests cover service redaction and malicious payload validation rather than the human-input emitter return contract.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add an emitter test that stubs KindlingService.emit, calls emitHumanInput, and asserts the returned ID is present in the emitted human_input observation if the API continues to promise a linkable ID.
items.minimumFixScope: Update human-input emitter and the observation contract/type exports consistently, plus tests for the public emitter contract.

items.title: queryMemories ignores default pagination for valid partial queries
items.recommendation: Normalise the query at the start of queryMemories, either by parsing with the MemoryQuery schema or by applying nullish defaults for include_superseded, limit, offset, sort_by, and sort_order before filtering and slicing.
items.reproduction: After saving one memory, call queryMemories({} as any). The filter includes the memory, but result.slice(undefined, NaN) returns an empty array and the returned limit/offset fields are undefined.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The MemoryStore tests build queries through queryDefaults, which supplies all defaulted fields and masks the missing normalisation in the store implementation.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a MemoryStore test that saves a memory and calls queryMemories({}) or the schema-valid equivalent, expecting one memory, limit 100, offset 0, and has_more false.
items.minimumFixScope: MemoryStore.queryMemories query normalisation and one regression test.

items.title: Promotion validation can throw TypeError instead of returning schema errors
items.recommendation: Only inspect reason/promoted_by after confirming they are strings, or use the parsed data when safeParse succeeds and otherwise return the collected Zod issues without additional field-specific trim checks.
items.reproduction: Call validatePromotionInput or promoteProposal with an object missing reason while require_reason is true. safeParse fails, then input.reason.trim() throws before the method can return validation errors.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The Zod violation test removes proposal_id only; the required string fields used after safeParse still exist, so no TypeError occurs.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add cases for missing and non-string reason/promoted_by that assert validatePromotionInput returns valid: false and promoteProposal rejects with Invalid promotion input rather than TypeError.
items.minimumFixScope: PromotionService.validatePromotionInput guard logic and focused validation tests.

items.title: Index paths can escape the storage root
items.recommendation: Validate index entry paths before use. Reject absolute paths, parent-directory traversal, and paths that do not resolve under storagePath; preferably derive the expected path from id/type and reject index entries that disagree with that canonical path.
items.reproduction: Create a storage directory with index.yaml containing a valid memory id and path: ../../victim.yaml, then call deleteMemory(id). The code resolves join(storagePath, '../../victim.yaml') and removes it if present.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The MemoryStore tests cover invalid memory ids before writing and type-change cleanup, but they only exercise indexes produced by saveMemory and do not load a malformed existing index path.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a MemoryStore test that writes an index.yaml with a valid id and a traversal path, creates a victim file outside storagePath, then asserts get/export/delete reject or ignore the entry and leave the victim file untouched.
items.minimumFixScope: MemoryIndexEntry validation plus MemoryStore read/delete/update path resolution.

items.title: OAuth nonce is not cleared on malformed or invalid callback state
items.recommendation: Wrap the missing_params and invalid_state redirects in clearNonce(), matching the other terminal callback paths.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests cover state encryption, next URL validation, cookie parsing, JWT verification, and BAuth exchange behavior, but there are no route-level tests for callback cookie clearing across error branches.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add route tests for /auth/callback that assert Set-Cookie clears oauth-nonce for missing code/state and undecryptable state values.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/docs-shell/app/auth/callback/route.ts plus a focused callback route test.

items.title: Default admin invites accept custom scopes but never persist them for activation
items.recommendation: Persist the accepted scopes on the default invite path, either by inserting an access_tokens entitlement row in the same transaction as the device code or by storing the pending scope grant in a table that /auth/device/poll consumes when minting the licence. Keep the response aligned with the actually persisted grant.
items.reproduction: POST /admin/invite with {"email":"alice@example.com","scopes":["preview","beta"]} and tokenOnly omitted. Complete the device activation flow. The activation licence will depend on existing active access_tokens rows rather than the scopes accepted by the invite request, so a first-time user falls back to the default scope set instead of receiving preview.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The admin invite tests only exercise the default ['beta'] scope and assert the response body; they do not send non-default scopes on the default invite path or verify that activation preserves them.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add an admin invite test for tokenOnly=false with scopes ['preview','beta'] that asserts the transaction includes a persisted grant carrying those scopes, plus a device-poll test showing the resulting licence includes the custom scopes for a first-time invited user.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/anvil-api/src/routes/admin.ts default invite transaction and the related admin/device activation tests.

items.title: OTP active-code cap can be bypassed by concurrent request bursts
items.recommendation: Move the cap enforcement into a single atomic database operation, for example an INSERT ... SELECT guarded by the active-code count under row/advisory lock or a serializable transaction. Consider adding a separate per-email or per-IP rate limit if this endpoint is exposed publicly.
