items.reproduction: For an active email with zero active OTP codes, send many POST /auth/otp/request calls concurrently. If the count queries race before inserts are visible, each request passes the activeCount < 3 check and executes insertOtpCode plus sendOtpCode.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing test stubs countActiveOtpCodes to return 3 in a single request and checks that no insert happens; it does not model concurrent requests where multiple handlers see the same pre-insert count.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test or query-level unit that drives several concurrent OTP request handlers with count initially below the cap and asserts no more than MAX_ACTIVE_CODES inserts/emails occur.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/anvil-api/src/routes/auth-otp.ts and the OTP query helper used to reserve an active code.

items.title: Refresh rotation consumes the old token before all failure-prone work completes
items.recommendation: Make refresh rotation atomic from the client contract's perspective. Generate/sign anything that can fail before consuming the old token where possible, then consume old token and insert the replacement in one database transaction. If the transaction fails, leave the old token unconsumed or return a clearly retryable state without burning the session.
items.reproduction: Mock findRefreshTokenByHash and findUserById to return valid rows, consumeRefreshToken to return true, and insertRefreshToken or signLicence to throw. The handler exits with an error after the old token has already been consumed and no replacement token has been returned.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The session tests cover happy-path rotation, pre-consumed reuse, revoked/expired tokens, inactive users, and a consume race, but they do not simulate failures after consumeRefreshToken succeeds.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add tests where insertRefreshToken and licence signing fail after a valid token lookup; assert the implementation does not leave the old token consumed without a replacement, or that the transaction rolls back.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/anvil-api/src/routes/auth-session.ts plus a transactional refresh-token rotation helper and failure-path tests.

items.title: Migration CLI depends on source-only migration files outside the packaged app
items.recommendation: Ship the migration SQL files alongside the built artifact and resolve from that shipped location, or include the required src/db/migrations and scripts directory in the package file set if the package scripts are intended to work from packaged output. Add a packaging-level check so the migrate script and its migration directory are validated together.
items.reproduction: Build or pack the package using the manifest file allow-list, then run the migrate script from the packaged artifact with DATABASE_URL set; the script resolves ../src/db/migrations relative to scripts/migrate.mjs, but that source directory is not included by the package file list.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: apps/anvil-api/src/__tests__/migrate.test.ts covers the migration runner using caller-supplied fixture directories; it does not execute apps/anvil-api/scripts/migrate.mjs or assert that packaged files include the migration SQL directory referenced by the CLI.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a package/artifact test that runs the built migration CLI against a fixture DATABASE_URL or mocked Pool from the same file layout used in release output, asserting that the resolved migrations directory exists and contains the SQL files.
items.minimumFixScope: Update apps/anvil-api/scripts/migrate.mjs and package/build packaging for apps/anvil-api so the CLI resolves migrations from an included artifact path; add a targeted artifact-layout test.

items.title: Hash validation exceptions can abort validation instead of returning a structured invalid result
items.recommendation: Catch HashValidationError inside validate or make validateHash return a false ValidationResult with a HASH_VALIDATION_FAILED issue when hash calculation fails. Reserve throwing for programmer errors if that is the intended contract and document/test it explicitly.
items.reproduction: Inject a hash validator that throws, then call await validator.validate(validPlan, { validateHash: true }); the promise rejects instead of resolving to { valid: false, issues: [...] }.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The hash tests cover successful matching, mismatch, skipped validator, and real hashing, but none cover a hash validator that throws or rejects.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that sets validator.setHashValidator(() => { throw new Error('boom'); }) and asserts validate(validPlan, { validateHash: true }) resolves to valid false with a structured issue rather than rejecting.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/core/src/validation/aps-validator.ts and the hash validation test block in packages/anvil/core/src/validation/aps-validator.test.ts

items.title: Gate type helper module is not exposed by the published package export map
items.recommendation: Either export these symbols from the root runtime index, add an explicit stable subpath export for the gate types/helpers, or mark the source module internal and remove the public API language to avoid implying consumer availability.
items.reproduction: After building the package, an external ESM consumer attempting to import a gate types/helper subpath from '@eddacraft/anvil-runtime' will be blocked by the package exports map because no './types/*' or './gate-types' subpath is declared.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked package export/import smoke tests were provided for this source group, and the package manifest contains no script that validates public subpath availability.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a package-level import smoke test that builds @eddacraft/anvil-runtime and imports the intended public gate type/helper entrypoint through the package name, not a relative source path.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/runtime/package.json export map and/or the runtime root index, plus an import smoke test for the intended public API.

items.title: Filter callback receives different path forms by mode
items.recommendation: Normalise the plan change path to fullPath before applying filter, and pass the same absolute path form to options.filter in both branches. If relative-path filtering is required, add an explicit separate option rather than overloading the same callback.
items.reproduction: Create a CheckContext with workspace_root '/repo', a plan proposed_change path 'src/a.ts', and options.filter = p => p.startsWith('/repo/'). getFilesFromContext returns [] even though normaliseTargetFiles(['src/a.ts'], '/repo', { filter, checkExists: false }) returns ['/repo/src/a.ts'].
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided for gate.types.ts, and repository search did not find tests covering normaliseTargetFiles or getFilesFromContext.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add runtime tests that call getFilesFromContext for targetFiles and for an equivalent plan.proposed_changes entry with the same filter callback, asserting identical results when checkExists is false.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/runtime/src/types/gate.types.ts plan-based branch plus focused tests for filter path normalisation.

items.title: Health E2E suite tests a local stub instead of the API package
items.recommendation: Change the health E2E tests to import the real @eddacraft/anvil-api app and request http://localhost/api/v1/health, keeping assertions tolerant of documented degraded states if the test environment lacks DB/signing configuration.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The health tests cover only the inline stub they define. The smoke test only asserts the route responds with 200 or 503 and does not validate the dedicated health contract shape beyond status being present.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Update apps/e2e/src/api/health.e2e.test.ts so all tests exercise the imported API app rather than a locally constructed Hono route, then assert the timestamp/404 behavior against that real app.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/e2e/src/api/health.e2e.test.ts

items.title: Task-only filters leave unrelated modules in the filtered result
items.recommendation: After applying task, confidence, and status filters that operate only on tasks, recompute filteredModules to modules containing at least one filtered task unless the API explicitly wants empty matched modules. At minimum, narrow modules when criteria.tasks is present.
items.reproduction: Load a multi-module plan such as packages/aps/examples/system-ecommerce/APS.md and call filterPlan(plan, { tasks: ['AUTH-001'] }); filtered.tasks contains one task, but filtered.modules still contains all modules unless another module-level criterion was also supplied. buildContextBundleText then renders unrelated modules with '*No tasks match the filter criteria.*'.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The task filtering test asserts only filtered.tasks length and IDs; it never checks filtered.modules or context bundle output for a task-only filter.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a filterPlan test for { tasks: ['AUTH-001'] } on a multi-module plan asserting filtered.modules contains only the module that owns AUTH-001, and add a context bundle test asserting unrelated modules are not emitted for task-only filters.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/aps/src/filter/index.ts plus focused tests in packages/aps/src/filter/filter.test.ts

items.title: As-built source glob references can escape the repository root
items.recommendation: Apply the same repository-root containment check before evaluating glob patterns. Reject absolute glob patterns and any glob whose static base resolves outside root, or validate every matched path is contained within root before accepting the reference.
items.reproduction: Create a governed As-built or Runbook document with a source reference containing a matching escape glob such as `../*`, then run `node scripts/docs/check-asbuilt-paths.mjs --no-baseline`; the glob branch can return no finding because it only checks that globby found at least one match.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked feature lists no tests. The existing docs-check shell coverage only verifies that the asbuilt-paths surface emits summaries and JSON; it does not cover escaping glob source references.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a fixture Runbook/As-built document with source references like `../*` and an in-repo glob, then assert the escape glob is an ERROR while the in-repo glob is accepted.
items.minimumFixScope: scripts/docs/check-asbuilt-paths.mjs resolveSourcePath glob handling and a focused docs-check fixture test

items.title: Documentation scripts rely on undeclared runtime packages
items.recommendation: Declare every bare package imported by scripts/docs/*.mjs in the root package.json devDependencies, or move the scripts into a package that declares those dependencies and invoke them through that package.
items.reproduction: Run a clean install layout where only declared direct dependencies are resolvable by the root package, then execute `pnpm docs:check` or `pnpm docs:index`; Node can fail during module resolution for the undeclared imports.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked feature lists no tests, and the existing docs-check shell tests exercise behaviour after module loading succeeds; they do not assert that bare imports in root scripts are declared direct dependencies.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a dependency-hygiene test that scans scripts/docs/*.mjs for bare import specifiers and fails when any non-node, non-workspace import is absent from package.json dependencies or devDependencies.
items.minimumFixScope: package.json dependency declaration update plus lockfile refresh if applicable

items.title: Metadata tables are accepted even when they are not immediately after the H1
items.recommendation: Change the table collection to enforce adjacency after the H1, allowing only ignorable whitespace/html/comment nodes if the markdown AST represents them, and throw a ParseError when the first required metadata table is not the next substantive top-level node. Then require the relationships table to immediately follow the metadata table under the same rule.
items.reproduction:
Parse a document shaped as `# Title

Intro text before metadata.

| Type | Authority | Owner | Status | Freshness |...` followed by the relationships table. The current implementation accepts it because it skips over non-table nodes after the H1.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing tests cover no tables after prose and a missing second table, but they do not include a case where valid-looking tables appear later after intervening prose.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that inserts prose between the H1 and an otherwise valid metadata table and expects parseDocGovernance to throw a ParseError mentioning the metadata table placement.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/docs-meta/src/parser/parse-metadata.ts plus a targeted parser test in packages/docs-meta/src/parser/parse-metadata.test.ts

items.title: Foreground scan-buffer test uses the caller's real fence store
items.recommendation: Pass a temp fence store in run_foreground_uses_configured_scan_buffer_service, for example tmp.path().join("state/intercept-fences.json"), before spawning run_foreground.
items.reproduction: On Unix: tmp=$(mktemp -d); mkdir -p "$tmp/anvil"; chmod 700 "$tmp/anvil"; printf 'not json\n' > "$tmp/anvil/intercept-fences.json"; XDG_STATE_HOME="$tmp" cargo test -p eddacraft-anvil-intercept run_foreground_uses_configured_scan_buffer_service -- --exact
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The affected test is the coverage. It validates scan-buffer service injection but does not assert that all daemon state paths are temp-scoped; the other run_foreground tests using with_fence_store_file do not protect this one.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Keep the existing test but add .with_fence_store_file(tmp.path().join("state/intercept-fences.json")); optionally add a helper that constructs foreground test opts so future tests cannot omit the fence store override.
items.minimumFixScope: One-line test setup change in crates/anvil-intercept/src/lib.rs, plus any formatting if needed.

items.title: Exported package version is stale relative to the published manifest
items.recommendation: Derive PACKAGE_VERSION from the manifest at build time or update it to match package.json as part of the release process. Add a test that asserts the exported metadata matches the package manifest.
items.reproduction: Build or import packages/edda-stack/src/index.ts and compare PACKAGE_VERSION with packages/edda-stack/package.json version; the exported constant is 0.1.0 while the manifest version is 0.7.3-beta.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests exercise config and contract modules directly. None import the root package entrypoint or assert PACKAGE_VERSION/PACKAGE_NAME metadata consistency.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add an index.test.ts that imports PACKAGE_VERSION from ./index.js and compares it with the version field parsed from ../package.json.
items.minimumFixScope: Update packages/edda-stack/src/index.ts metadata handling and add a focused root entrypoint metadata test.

items.title: Send migration union accepts contradictory dryRun payloads as real sends
items.recommendation: Make the real-send branch explicitly reject dryRun, for example by adding dryRun: z.never().optional() to SendResponseSchema or by using a stricter/discriminated shape that preserves the intended absent-field contract.
items.reproduction: SendMigrationResponseSchema.safeParse({ dryRun: true, source: 'manual', total: 1, sent: 1, failed: 0, results: [] }).success returns true via SendResponseSchema unless the send branch explicitly rejects the discriminator field.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided for this feature, and directory inspection found no package-local test/spec files under packages/shared/admin-contracts to exercise invalid discriminator combinations.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a Vitest case asserting that SendMigrationResponseSchema rejects a payload containing dryRun: true together with the real-send fields, and still accepts the valid real-send shape without dryRun.
items.minimumFixScope: Update SendResponseSchema or SendMigrationResponseSchema in packages/shared/admin-contracts/src/index.ts and add focused schema coverage for the migration response discriminator.

items.title: Admin contract schemas have no package-local regression coverage
items.recommendation: Add package-local Vitest coverage for representative valid and invalid payloads across the exported response schemas, with emphasis on timestamp coercion, ID coercion, nullable fields, drift responses, and send-migration branch discrimination.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature metadata lists no tests, and directory inspection found no test/spec files under packages/shared/admin-contracts.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Create packages/shared/admin-contracts/src/index.test.ts with parse and safeParse cases for InviteResponseSchema, RevokeResponseSchema, SendMigrationResponseSchema, DriftDiffResponseSchema, WaitlistResponseSchema, AuditResponseSchema, and ShowResponseSchema.
items.minimumFixScope: Add package-local schema tests under packages/shared/admin-contracts/src and ensure the package test script runs them.

items.title: No first-class tests exercise the common adapter registry surface
items.recommendation: Add a focused Vitest suite for packages/adapters/src/common/registry.ts using a minimal SpecToolAdapter mock, or remove the common registry surface if it is obsolete and route consumers to the tested base registry.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included test file targets packages/adapters/src/base/registry.ts, not packages/adapters/src/common/registry.ts, so regressions in the common registry would not fail that suite.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Create packages/adapters/src/common/__tests__/registry.test.ts covering register duplicate rejection, unregister/getAdapter/listSupportedFormats, singleton reuse/clear isolation, and detectFormat's returned value.
items.minimumFixScope: Add tests for packages/adapters/src/common/registry.ts and clarify or align detectFormat expectations in those tests.

items.title: Commented-out imports are treated as real dependency edges
items.recommendation: Use a TypeScript/JavaScript parser for TS/JS files, or at minimum strip comments before regex extraction while preserving line numbers. Add explicit negative tests for line comments, block comments, and string literals containing import-like text.
items.reproduction: Create a file in a detected layer containing only `// import { db } from '../repositories/db.js';`, then run architecture analysis over it with a target path that maps to a disallowed layer. The regex scan will emit an edge even though there is no runtime dependency.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The edge-detector tests cover normal import, export, dynamic import, require, missing files, and no-import files, but they do not include commented-out or string-literal import text.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add an `extractImports` test where a file contains `// import x from './x.js'`, `/* require('./y.js') */`, and a string value containing `import ... from`; assert that no edges are returned for those lines.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/core/src/architecture/edge-detector.ts plus edge-detector tests.

items.title: inferBaseline save option is documented but ignored by baseline creation path
items.recommendation: Clarify the API. If `save: false` is meant to be dry-run, construct the baseline with the pure `createBaseline` helper instead of `BaselineManager.create`, and only call `save` when requested. If persistence is intentional, remove or rename the option and update the interface comment.
items.reproduction: Call `inferBaseline(tmpDir, { save: false })`; `.anvil/architecture.json` is still created, as asserted by the included test.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The test suite covers the current behavior and therefore would fail if the option were fixed without updating test expectations; it does not test the contract implied by the option comment.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Replace the current `save: false` assertion with one that calls `inferBaseline(tmpDir, { save: false })` and expects `.anvil/architecture.json` not to exist, if dry-run behavior is intended.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/core/src/architecture/analyzer.ts and the inferBaseline tests.

items.title: Dependency-cruiser config is generated as CommonJS in ESM package scope
items.recommendation: Change `DC_CONFIG_FILENAME` to `dependency-cruiser.cjs` for CommonJS output, or emit ESM config syntax and verify dependency-cruiser supports that mode. Update regeneration/path tests to assert the chosen extension and module format.

items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/core/src/architecture/dc-generator.ts and dc-generator tests; update any callers expecting `.anvil/dependency-cruiser.js`.

items.title: DashboardRenderer renders @json-render Renderer without required provider context
items.recommendation: Wrap Renderer with @json-render/react JSONUIProvider, or with StateProvider, VisibilityProvider, ActionProvider, and ValidationProvider, using empty defaults where this package does not expose handlers/state. Add props for initial state and action handlers if consumers need them.
items.reproduction: Render <DashboardRenderer spec={validSpec} /> with one of the included valid dashboard specs. Validation succeeds, then the nested Renderer is mounted without the json-render providers it expects.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The tests call validateSpec and inspect template structure only. They do not import DashboardRenderer or mount a valid spec through the React renderer path.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a React render test that mounts DashboardRenderer with a minimal valid Stack/Heading spec and asserts the heading text is rendered without a role=alert render error.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/libs/render/src/dashboard-renderer.tsx plus a focused DashboardRenderer render test

items.title: Prototype-pollution protection is shallow for arbitrary APS metadata
items.recommendation: Replace safeRecord(z.unknown()) with a recursive safe unknown/object schema for untrusted metadata fields, or recursively walk unknown values in safeRecord.superRefine and reject forbidden keys at any depth.
items.reproduction: An APS plan with metadata: { safe: JSON.parse('{"__proto__":{"polluted":true}}') } passes the top-level safeRecord checks because the only metadata key is 'safe' and the nested value is z.unknown.

items.title: Package metadata still advertises zero dependencies while shipping runtime dependencies
items.recommendation: Update the package description and entrypoint comment to describe the real dependency contract, or move any truly type-only dependency to devDependencies if the intent is only to avoid non-zod runtime dependencies.

items.title: Debug object payloads bypass redaction
items.recommendation: Sanitize object payloads before logging. A pragmatic fix is to JSON-stringify with a safe replacer/redactor for known secret-bearing keys and token-like string values, then log the sanitized representation; handle circular structures defensively.
items.reproduction: Call createDebugger('api')('request', { authorization: 'Bearer secret-token-value', apiKey: 'sk-test-secret' }) with ANVIL_DEBUG=1. The object is logged unchanged.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests exercise debug.ts or verify that object payloads are redacted; existing email/token/licence tests do not cover debug logging.

items.minimumFixScope: apps/anvil-api/src/lib/debug.ts plus a focused unit test for object payload redaction.

items.title: Beta invite schema accepts unvalidated activation URLs
items.recommendation: Reuse the same HTTPS URL validator for betaInvitePropsSchema.activateUrl, or extract a shared schema for email-rendered links. Consider adding the same userinfo, whitespace, control-character, and length caps used for release-announcement URLs.

items.title: AppendOutcome is not exported from the library surface
items.recommendation: Re-export AppendOutcome from lib.rs alongside the other writer API types, e.g. `pub use writer::{AppendOutcome, RolloverPolicy, WitnessWriter, WriterError};`.

items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included concurrency test calls `writer.append(&line).unwrap()` and ignores the return value, so inference is enough and no downstream-style import or wrapper signature exercises the missing export.

items.title: Crate-level docs advertise stale witness contracts
items.recommendation: Update the crate-level docs to say the baselined anchor is the bare `GENESIS-BASELINED` value and that the cutoff commit belongs in the `cutoff_commit` field.

items.minimumFixScope: Documentation correction in crates/anvil-witness/src/lib.rs, plus a small anchor-contract test if not already covered elsewhere.

items.title: TraceContext object path can emit an invalid traceparent header
items.recommendation: Validate the object path before attaching, either by parsing traceparent.header or by formatting from traceId, parentId, and flags with formatTraceparent. Prefer deriving the header from validated fields so header cannot disagree with the rest of the context.
items.reproduction: attachTraceparentToEnvelope({ jsonrpc: '2.0', id: 1 }, { traceId: '0af7651916cd43dd8448eb211c80319c', parentId: 'b7ad6b7169203331', flags: 1, sampled: true, header: 'not-a-traceparent' }) returns an envelope with traceparent: 'not-a-traceparent' instead of rejecting or canonicalizing.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing attachTraceparentToEnvelope test only passes a string traceparent, so it exercises the validating branch and never covers the TraceContext object branch.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that passes a TraceContext-shaped object with an invalid header to attachTraceparentToEnvelope and asserts it throws, or add a test that passes mismatched header/fields and asserts the emitted header is canonicalized from the fields.
items.minimumFixScope: Update attachTraceparentToEnvelope in packages/anvil/observability/src/traceparent.ts and add a focused regression test in packages/anvil/observability/src/traceparent.test.ts.

items.title: BMAD serializer leaves acceptance criteria in the user story heading
items.recommendation: Extract and remove the acceptance criteria suffix before writing the heading. Keep a separate clean title variable and criteria array so the heading contains only the story title.
items.reproduction: Parse a BMAD story with US-01, an As a/I want/so that block, and numbered Acceptance Criteria, then serialize the resulting APS plan. The generated user story heading includes the '- Acceptance criteria: ...' suffix as well as a criteria list.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The visible BMAD tests cover user stories without acceptance criteria and general serializer success, but they do not assert serialized output for user stories that include acceptance criteria.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a parse-then-serialize BMAD user story test with numbered acceptance criteria and assert the heading excludes 'Acceptance criteria' while the criteria list is present.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/adapters/src/bmad/serializer.ts user story rendering.

items.title: BMAD parse conversion drops collected errors and warnings
items.recommendation: Make bmadToAPS return both the plan and accumulated diagnostics, or throw/return a failed ParseResult when errors.length > 0. Pass warnings through createParseSuccess for non-fatal diagnostics such as NO_CHANGES.
items.reproduction: Parse a valid agent YAML whose agent.metadata.id is '../outside.md'. safePath throws, bmadToAPS pushes INVALID_PATH, then returns a plan; BMADFormatAdapter.parse returns success without errors and without the agent change.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests assert successful parsing for valid BMAD documents and generic parser edge cases, but they do not assert that BMAD conversion diagnostics are surfaced on ParseResult when safePath rejects structured YAML fields or when bmadToAPS creates NO_CHANGES.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a BMAD adapter parse test with structured YAML containing an invalid path and assert result.success is false with INVALID_PATH, plus a no-change markdown BMAD test that asserts result.warnings contains NO_CHANGES if success remains valid.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/adapters/src/bmad/parser.ts and packages/adapters/src/bmad/format-adapter.ts parse result plumbing.

items.title: BMAD input size guard checks UTF-16 length instead of byte length
items.recommendation: Use Buffer.byteLength(content, 'utf8') for the BMAD size check, matching parseGeneric, and keep the error wording as a byte limit.
items.reproduction: Build content from Math.floor(MAX_INPUT_SIZE / 4) + 1 emoji characters. Buffer.byteLength(content, 'utf8') exceeds 2 MiB while content.length stays below or equal to the limit, so parseBMADDocument does not throw the maximum size error.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked generic parser test covers the multibyte byte-limit case for parseGeneric only. The BMAD edge tests cover large content around 500 KB and do not include a multibyte input that exceeds the byte limit while passing .length.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a BMAD parser size-guard test mirroring packages/adapters/src/generic/__tests__/parser.test.ts for multibyte content over MAX_INPUT_SIZE bytes.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/adapters/src/bmad/parser.ts size check plus a BMAD-specific regression test.

items.title: Warning result consistency check ignores most summary counters
items.recommendation: Recompute the full expected summary from result.warnings, then compare total, suppressed, blocking, every expected category, and all known severities in both directions. Alternatively replace the helper body with a comparison against createWarningResult(result.warnings).summary.
items.reproduction: Build a WarningResult with one severity='error' unsuppressed warning, summary.total=1, summary.bySeverity={}, summary.byCategory={}, summary.suppressed=0, and summary.blocking=0. validateWarningResultConsistency returns true even though bySeverity.error and blocking are wrong.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature lists no linked tests, and no included test evidence exercises malformed WarningResult summaries with omitted severity keys or incorrect blocking/suppressed/category counts.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a warning.schema test that mutates each summary field from createWarningResult output, including deleting bySeverity.error and setting blocking to 0 for an unsuppressed error, and asserts validateWarningResultConsistency returns false.
items.minimumFixScope: Update validateWarningResultConsistency in packages/anvil/core/src/contracts/schemas/warning.schema.ts and add focused unit coverage for inconsistent summary fields.

items.title: Git status path conversion treats sibling paths as inside the workspace
items.recommendation: Resolve both workspaceRoot and filePath, compute relative(), and only accept the relative path when it is non-empty, does not start with '..', and is not absolute. Otherwise return the original path or reject/filter it explicitly according to the API contract.
items.reproduction: With workspaceRoot '/repo', call getFileStatus('/repo-other/file.ts'). toRelativePath returns '../repo-other/file.ts', so git is invoked as git status --porcelain -- ../repo-other/file.ts from /repo instead of treating the input as outside the workspace.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The git-status tests only cover paths truly under the workspace root and quoted rename parsing. They do not cover sibling prefixes such as /repo-other or workspace roots with shared string prefixes.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a GitStatusChecker test for workspaceRoot '/repo' and filePath '/repo-other/file.ts' asserting gitExec is not called with '../repo-other/file.ts', or that the method rejects/returns a safe outside-workspace status per the intended contract.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/runtime/src/watch/git-status.ts toRelativePath path containment logic plus sibling-prefix regression coverage.

items.title: Restarting the orchestrator registers duplicate watcher listeners
items.recommendation: Store bound listener methods on the orchestrator instance and unregister them in stop(), or register them once in the constructor. Add removeListener/off support in stop before allowing restart.
items.reproduction: Create a WatchOrchestrator with multiAgent disabled and a test FileWatcher/mocked chokidar, call start(), stop(), start(), then emit one FileWatcher change event. The onEvent/action path is invoked twice and changesDetected increments by 2 for one change.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included FileWatcher restart test only asserts the lower-level watcher can restart after stop. There is no orchestrator restart test and no assertion that status/change handlers are registered only once across start-stop-start.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add an orchestrator test that starts, stops, starts again, triggers one FileWatcher change, advances the debounce, and asserts only one change/action event and changesDetected === 1.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/runtime/src/watch/orchestrator.ts listener lifecycle handling plus a focused orchestrator restart regression test.

items.title: Plugin metadata version is stale relative to the package version
items.recommendation: Keep plugin.meta.version in sync with package.json, preferably by deriving it during build or adding a test that asserts the metadata matches the manifest.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included rule tests exercise individual rules only; they do not import the plugin entrypoint or assert package metadata.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add an index-level test that imports package.json and src/index.ts, then expects plugin.meta.version to equal packageJson.version.
items.minimumFixScope: Update src/index.ts metadata and add a small entrypoint metadata test.

items.title: CWD restoration can occur before the final directory change and still satisfy the rule
items.recommendation: Track the ordering of process.chdir calls and require the last relevant chdir to restore a saved cwd variable, or track each chdir-changing block/hook and ensure its matching cleanup occurs after the mutation.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing cwd tests cover multiple chdir calls only when the final call restores originalCwd; they do not include a restoration followed by another directory change.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add an invalid RuleTester case where process.chdir(originalCwd) is followed by process.chdir('/tmp/b') and expect missingRestoration.
items.minimumFixScope: Update require-cwd-restoration state tracking and add focused RuleTester cases for restoration order.

items.title: Mock cleanup detection accepts comments and strings as real restoreAllMocks calls
items.recommendation: Detect vi.restoreAllMocks() via AST traversal within the afterEach callback body, or maintain callback-depth state while visiting CallExpression nodes, so only executable calls count as cleanup.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The current invalid tests include an afterEach with vi.clearAllMocks(), but none include restoreAllMocks text inside a comment or string literal.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add invalid cases where afterEach contains a comment and a string literal with `vi.restoreAllMocks(` while vi.mock or vi.spyOn is used.
items.minimumFixScope: Replace the regex-based afterEach source scan in require-mock-cleanup and add targeted false-negative tests.

items.title: Real-send migration responses accept and strip the dryRun discriminator
items.recommendation: Make the real-send branch explicitly reject the discriminator, for example by adding dryRun: z.never().optional() to SendResponseSchema or by using a strict/passthrough-plus-refine strategy that rejects any present dryRun field without unintentionally breaking allowed additive fields.
items.reproduction: SendMigrationResponseSchema.parse({ dryRun: true, source: 'manual', total: 1, sent: 1, failed: 0, results: [] }) succeeds instead of rejecting the invalid discriminator.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided for this package, and the current schema has no regression coverage proving that discriminator-bearing real-send payloads are rejected.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a vitest case asserting SendMigrationResponseSchema rejects real-send-shaped payloads when dryRun is present, including dryRun: true and dryRun: false.

items.title: Generated Vercel ignore command leaves path arguments shell-interpreted
items.recommendation: Validate rootDirectory and extraWatchPaths with the same conservative character policy used for productionBranch, or render every path with a shell-quoting helper that correctly escapes single quotes. Prefer validation for repo-relative paths because these values should be simple workspace paths.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The tests cover shell-metacharacter rejection for productionBranch only. They do not exercise rootDirectory or extraWatchPaths containing spaces, quotes, semicolons, or command substitutions.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add VercelApp tests that reject rootDirectory and extraWatchPaths values such as "apps/web; echo injected" and "docs/public/it's" unless they are safely quoted in the generated ignoreCommand.

items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing CORS test checks only that eddacraft.ai and www.eddacraft.ai are included; it does not assert that arbitrary Vercel origins are excluded.

items.title: domainImports accepts import IDs for a different domain
items.recommendation: Parse the import ID after the project prefix and require the extracted domain to exactly match the domainImports key. Keep supporting both project-only and team-prefixed forms.

items.title: Registry-load docs still promise hard failure for missing registries after embedded fallback
items.recommendation: Update the crate-level registry-load section and the trailing test note to distinguish missing/unresolvable overrides, which fall back to the embedded catalogue, from malformed resolved registry files, which still return GenericFailure.

items.title: General rate limiter is fixed-window despite documenting sliding-window semantics
items.recommendation: Either implement actual sliding-window accounting, such as storing recent request timestamps or bucketed rolling counters, or change the documentation/name to state fixed-window semantics so callers tune limits accordingly.
items.reproduction: With windowMs=60000 and max=60, send 60 requests near the end of a bucket and 60 more immediately after resetAt; all 120 can pass within a short real-time interval, which a true sliding window would reject.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked tests cover adminRateLimit and traceContext only. No included test exercises rateLimiter timing around a window boundary or asserts sliding-window behaviour.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a rateLimiter test using fake timers that exhausts max requests, advances to just after resetAt, and verifies a true sliding-window implementation still rejects until the earlier requests age out.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/anvil-api/src/middleware/rate-limit.ts plus a focused unit test for boundary-window behaviour.

items.title: Dual-run parity harness never executes the TypeScript engine
items.recommendation: Wire run_dual to the real TypeScript architecture engine output, or rename/scope the harness so it is not treated as parity coverage until that integration exists. Once wired, compare normalized records from both engines for representative clean, violating, and mixed projects.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing tests explicitly codify the placeholder: ts_placeholder_always_empty expects the TS side to be empty, and comparison tests only exercise synthetic Vec inputs rather than invoking the real JS engine.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add an integration test that creates a fixture known to trigger the JS architecture check, runs both engines through run_dual, and asserts matches is true with no discrepancies after both sides report the same normalized violation records.
items.minimumFixScope: crates/anvil-kernel/tests/dual_run.rs and the test support needed to invoke or fixture the real TypeScript engine output

items.title: Generic package generator emits packages under the wrong npm scope
items.recommendation: Derive the npm scope from the repository convention or make it an explicit validated option, and default it to @eddacraft for this workspace. Update the platform/shared import path logic accordingly.

items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided for this generator, and the generated placeholder tests only assert `expect(true).toBe(true)` after generation.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a generator unit test that runs the package generator for `packages/shared/storage` and asserts the emitted package.json `name`, generated JSDoc `@module`, and import path all use the expected @eddacraft namespace.
items.minimumFixScope: Change `normalizeOptions` in `tools/generators/src/generators/package/generator.ts` and add generator-output tests for package naming.

items.title: Generated Nx project names collide across package directories
items.recommendation: Include the directory scope in `projectName` for scoped directories, for example `platform-auth` and `shared-auth`, or derive the project name from the final import path in a deterministic way.
items.reproduction: Run the package generator twice with `{ directory: 'packages/platform', name: 'auth' }` and `{ directory: 'packages/shared', name: 'auth' }`; both emitted project.json files contain `"name": "auth"`.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests cover multiple generated packages with the same leaf name in different directories.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a generator test that creates platform and shared packages with the same name and asserts their emitted project.json names are unique and stable.
items.minimumFixScope: Update `normalizeOptions` in `tools/generators/src/generators/package/generator.ts` and add a collision-focused generator test.

items.title: Unescaped generator inputs can produce uncompilable TypeScript
items.recommendation: Validate names against the intended kebab-case identifier/path contract before writing files, derive PascalCase only from validated segments, and escape all values that are emitted into TypeScript string literals or comments using a small code-generation helper.
items.reproduction: Generate a gate check with `name=policy.audit` or `description=owner's gate`; the generator writes TypeScript that cannot parse or typecheck.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked generator tests exercise invalid names, punctuation, quotes, or comment terminators. The generated scaffold tests are written after the bad interpolation, so they do not protect the generator itself.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add generator tests covering quoted descriptions, dotted names, slash-containing names, and valid kebab-case names; assert invalid inputs fail before files are written and valid inputs produce parseable TypeScript.
items.minimumFixScope: Add input validation and TypeScript literal/comment escaping in the gate-check generator, then apply the same escaping helper to generated descriptions in package generators.

items.title: Context bundles can count scope-matched tasks that are never rendered
items.recommendation: When building bundles, include the owning module for every filtered task, even if the module did not independently match module-level criteria, or add an explicit ungrouped matchedTasks section. Keep the summary count and rendered task details derived from the same set.
items.reproduction: Create a plan with module id core/scope CORE containing task CORE-001 with Scopes: AUTH. Call filterPlan(plan, { scopes: ['AUTH'] }) and then buildContextBundleJSON. The summary reports one task, while modules is empty or lacks that task because the owning module did not pass the module-scope filter.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Existing filter tests assert cross-scope task matching, and bundle tests assert summary/module presence for current fixtures, but there is no fixture where a matching task belongs to a non-matching module.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a focused fixture with a CORE module containing an AUTH-scoped task, filter by AUTH, build both JSON and text bundles, and assert the matched task appears in the rendered task details as well as the summary.
items.minimumFixScope: Context bundle generation in packages/aps/src/filter/context-bundle.ts, with possible adjustment to filterPlan module inclusion semantics.

items.title: Publish target points at dist but package entrypoints point at dist again
items.recommendation: Choose one layout and make it consistent. Either publish from the project root and include dist files, or publish from dist with a generated dist/package.json whose main/types/exports point to ./index.js, ./parser/index.js, etc. Add a pack/import smoke test for the package root used by nx-release-publish.
items.reproduction: Build the package, place or copy the current package.json into packages/aps/dist as the release manifest, then pack/publish from packages/aps/dist. Importing the package resolves the root export to a missing ./dist/index.js inside the published package root.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The tests exercise source imports and package functionality, but none build the package, pack from the configured packageRoot, and import the packed artifact through package.json exports.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: After nx build, run npm pack or pnpm pack from the configured packageRoot in a temp directory, install the tarball into a fixture project, and assert imports from @eddacraft/anvil-aps and each documented subpath resolve.
items.minimumFixScope: Package release metadata for packages/aps: package.json entrypoints, project.json packageRoot, and any build step that prepares dist/package.json.

items.title: Concurrent successful locks for different tasks can overwrite each other in state.json
items.recommendation: Serialize state-file mutations with a project-level state lock, or implement an atomic compare-and-retry loop that rereads and merges on write conflicts. Keep per-task lock files for ownership, but protect the shared state map as a single mutable resource.
items.reproduction: Create two TaskLocker instances against the same temp project and run Promise.all([lockerA.lock('TEST-001'), lockerB.lock('TEST-002')]) repeatedly or with a small delay injected between readStateFile and writeStateFile. Observe both lock calls can report success while .anvil/state.json contains only one of the two task records.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing concurrency tests cover many contenders for the same task, which the per-task lock file handles. They do not cover concurrent successful locks for different task IDs that both write the shared state file.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a TaskLocker test that concurrently locks TEST-001, TEST-002, and TEST-003 with different users, asserts all calls succeed, then reads state.json and verifies all three task entries are present with the expected locked_by values.
items.minimumFixScope: State module write path: updateTaskState plus TaskLocker lock/unlock/complete callers that mutate .anvil/state.json.

items.title: Template generation script omits the public action template
items.recommendation: Update the script to write actions-template.md and log it. If the templates directory is intended to contain all variants, generate minimal/standard/full files consistently for actions too. Add a script-level test or smoke command that verifies every TemplateBundle key is emitted.

items.title: Ports package contract says contracts-only but exports core-dependent types
items.recommendation: Either move APSPlan and WarningResult into the contracts layer and import them from there, or update the package description/module documentation to make @eddacraft/anvil-core an intentional public dependency. Prefer the former if ports are meant to remain a boundary package.

items.title: Public InterruptReason can bypass the 1-based line invariant
items.recommendation: Make the invariant unrepresentable or enforce it at the boundary: use a private `InterruptReason` constructor, store `line` as `Option<NonZeroU32>`, or at minimum have `interrupt_reason_to_diagnostic` reject or normalise `Some(0)` before building `Location`.
items.reproduction: Implement an `InterceptRule` whose `evaluate` returns `RuleDecision::Interrupt(InterruptReason { rule_id: "r".into(), message: "m".into(), line: Some(0) })`, then call the default `diagnostics`; the returned diagnostic has `location.line == Some(0)`.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing test only proves `RuleDecision::interrupt_at(..., 0)` panics; it does not cover direct construction of the public `InterruptReason` struct or the default diagnostic conversion path.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test with a stub rule that returns a directly constructed `InterruptReason { line: Some(0), .. }` and assert the diagnostics path cannot emit `location.line == Some(0)`.
items.minimumFixScope: `crates/anvil-intercept-rules/src/lib.rs` API/invariant handling plus the embedded tests for default diagnostic conversion.

items.title: format=text is documented as valid but success responses only describe JSON
items.recommendation: Either remove 'text' from the OpenAPI HTTP format parameter or add text/plain 200 response content for every operation that accepts format=text, keeping JSON and text response contracts distinct.

items.suggestedRegressionTest: Generate the OpenAPI document and assert that every operation accepting format=text either has a text/plain 200 response content entry or does not advertise text as an allowed format.

items.title: parseSeverity cannot honour an explicit undefined default for invalid input
items.recommendation: Either change the implementation to distinguish omitted default from an explicitly supplied undefined, such as using arguments.length, or simplify the contract by removing the undefined-default overload and documentation. Add a regression test for invalid input with an explicit undefined default.
items.reproduction: parseSeverity(123, undefined) evaluates to 'info', contrary to the documented example and overload intent.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: severity.test.ts checks valid values with undefined default but does not check invalid strings or non-string values when defaultValue is explicitly undefined.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: expect(parseSeverity(123, undefined)).toBeUndefined(); and expect(parseSeverity('invalid', undefined)).toBeUndefined(); if the documented contract is retained.

items.title: validateRelativePath can return an absolute path after accepting a leading backslash
items.recommendation: Reject leading backslashes, drive-letter paths, and UNC-style paths before normalisation, or normalise separators first and then perform both POSIX and win32 absolute/escape checks. Add tests for leading backslash, drive-letter, UNC, null byte, upward traversal, and safe nested relative paths.
items.reproduction: On POSIX: validateRelativePath(String.raw`\tmp\payload`) passes the checks and returns `/tmp/payload`. A UNC-style input such as String.raw`\\server\share` similarly passes the pre-conversion checks and becomes slash-rooted output.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests cover git operations and severity parsing only; no included path-safety tests exercise validateRelativePath with backslash-prefixed or Windows-style inputs.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add path-safety tests asserting validateRelativePath(String.raw`\tmp\payload`), validateRelativePath(String.raw`C:\tmp\payload`), and validateRelativePath(String.raw`\\server\share`) all throw, while `dir/file.txt` still returns `dir/file.txt`.
items.minimumFixScope: Update validateRelativePath in packages/anvil/core/src/utils/path-safety.ts and add focused tests for cross-platform absolute path forms.

items.title: Structured debug data bypasses log sanitisation
items.recommendation: Sanitise structured data before logging, for example by recursively redacting string leaves and safely serialising plain objects, or by logging a sanitised JSON representation with circular-reference handling. Keep Error and string handling covered by the same sanitizer path.
items.reproduction: Set ANVIL_DEBUG=1 and call debug('config', 'loaded', { token: 'sk-secretvalue1234567890', note: 'ok\nforged' }); the object path is logged raw rather than through sanitizeForLog.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No included debug tests assert sanitisation behaviour for string data, Error data, or object data; the existing tests are limited to git operations and severity parsing.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Spy on console.debug with ANVIL_DEBUG enabled and assert object payloads containing token-like strings, newlines, and ANSI escapes are emitted only in sanitised form.
items.minimumFixScope: Update the non-string data branch in packages/anvil/core/src/utils/debug.ts and add focused debug logger tests.

Also ensure generated paths remain under the intended checks directory.

items.recommendation: Add a ./concurrency export pointing at dist/concurrency/index.js and dist/concurrency/index.d.ts, or change getHookSetupCommand and docs to use the root export consistently.

items.title: File-backed cache and queue updates can lose concurrent writes
items.recommendation: Use a single per-index/per-queue file lock around every read-modify-write path, not just join. For the cache, either lock index.json during set/invalidate/cleanup/maybeEvict/get stat updates or use append/merge semantics that re-read and merge before save.
items.reproduction: For cache: create two FileCacheProvider instances for the same workspace, call set on different keys concurrently from an empty index, then create a fresh provider and read both keys; one can be missing from index.json. For queue: interleave leave reading [A,B], join writing [A,B,C], then leave writing [B]; C is dropped.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The cache tests cover single-instance persistence and stats, and the queue tests cover sequential join/leave/status/priority behaviours. They do not create multiple providers/managers that mutate the same file concurrently.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add concurrent multi-instance tests for FileCacheProvider.set with distinct keys and QueueManager join/leave interleavings, asserting no entries are lost.
items.minimumFixScope: FileCacheProvider index mutations, QueueManager leave/status cleanup mutations, and focused concurrent regression tests.

items.title: Expired or stale lock takeover can grant the same lock to multiple agents
items.recommendation: Guard forceAcquire with the same exclusive sentinel used by createLock, and after acquiring the sentinel re-read the lock file to confirm it is still expired/stale and still the lock that was observed before replacing it.
items.reproduction: Create an expired lock, then start two LockManager instances with different agent IDs and call acquire for the same type/resource at the same time. Both can return acquired true because forceAcquire is not guarded by the .creating sentinel used for new locks.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing expired-lock test waits for expiry and then performs a single takeover; it does not race two takeover attempts against the same expired lock.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a concurrent expired-lock takeover test that starts two agents simultaneously and asserts exactly one acquire call succeeds.
items.minimumFixScope: LockManager.acquire/forceAcquire takeover path and one concurrent regression test.

items.title: Create output does not match the script's documented JSON contract
items.recommendation: Either change the emitted JSON to `{ id, hashed_key: hashedKey }` or update the contract and all consumers to expect `hashedKey`. Prefer snake_case here because the documented field mirrors the database column name.
items.reproduction: Run `admin-key-manage.mjs create` with valid database/env inputs and inspect stdout; the JSON contains `hashedKey`, not `hashed_key`.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature lists no linked tests, and there is no included test asserting the create stdout shape.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a script-level test or mocked integration test that exercises `create` and asserts stdout contains `id` and `hashed_key` exactly as documented.
items.minimumFixScope: Change the create stdout object and add coverage for the output schema.

items.title: Symlink escape checks can be bypassed by swapping paths after validation
items.recommendation: Avoid check-then-use path validation for security-sensitive filesystem writes/deletes. Use descriptor-based operations where possible, open parent directories safely, reject symlinks with lstat immediately before mutation, and/or constrain this provider to private base directories not writable by untrusted concurrent actors. For writes, consider writing to a newly created temporary file opened with flags that do not follow existing symlinks, then atomically renaming only after validating the containing directory.
items.reproduction: Create a writable baseDir with a victim path inside it. Start storage.write('victim', data), and between resolvePath returning and fs.writeFile executing, replace baseDir/victim with a symlink to a file outside baseDir. The write operation can follow the symlink and modify the outside file.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Existing symlink tests create the malicious symlink before calling the API, so resolvePath sees and rejects it. They do not simulate a path being swapped after validation and before mutation.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test-only hook or injectable filesystem adapter that pauses after resolvePath during write/delete, swaps the checked path to a symlink outside baseDir, then verifies the outside file is not modified or deleted.
items.minimumFixScope: Update FileStorage mutation paths to avoid symlink-following TOCTOU windows, or explicitly narrow and enforce the API contract so baseDir must not be concurrently writable by untrusted actors.

items.title: Baseline violation IDs can collide for distinct file paths
items.recommendation: Generate the ID from a collision-resistant hash of a structured tuple containing fromFile, toFile, and line, or store the raw tuple and compare all fields instead of a lossy sanitised string.
items.reproduction: createViolationId('src/a-b.ts', 'src/c.ts', 1) === createViolationId('src/a_b.ts', 'src/c.ts', 1).
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included baseline and edge-detector tests exercise ID equality for exact matches, but they do not include two different paths that normalise to the same ID.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test asserting createViolationId returns different values for paths that differ only by punctuation, and that baseline comparison treats the second violation as new.
items.minimumFixScope: Change createViolationId and any tests that assert the old textual format; preserve deterministic output.

items.title: Explicit Rego rules do not escape layer names in string literals
items.recommendation: Use the same string-literal escaping helper for rule.from, rule.to, rule.severity, and comment-bearing names where they are emitted into generated source, or emit these comparisons through JSON.stringify to produce valid quoted literals.
items.reproduction: Define a layer named ui"x and a forbidden rule from ui"x to data; generateRegoPolicy emits v.from_layer == "ui"x", which is not valid Rego.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included compiler tests only check file generation and hash consistency; the Rego generator tests present in the repository only use simple identifier-like layer names and substring assertions, not names requiring escaping or an OPA parse of the generated policy.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a Rego generator test with quoted or backslash-containing layer names and assert the generated policy parses under OPA or contains correctly escaped string literals.
items.minimumFixScope: Escape every user-controlled string interpolated into Rego source, not just rule.message.

items.title: Template defaults are returned as mutable shared layer objects
items.recommendation: Deep-clone template defaults before returning them, including nested arrays and layer objects. structuredClone is sufficient for these plain data records.
items.reproduction: const a = getTemplateDefaults('starter'); a.lib.depends_on.push('x'); const b = createDefinitionFromTemplate('starter'); b.layers.lib.depends_on now contains 'x'.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing merge/create tests assert returned shapes and non-mutation of the input definition, but they do not mutate a returned template and then request the same template again.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that mutates the layers returned by getTemplateDefaults or createDefinitionFromTemplate, then calls createDefinitionFromTemplate again and verifies the built-in defaults are unchanged.
items.minimumFixScope: Deep-clone in getTemplateDefaults so mergeWithTemplate and createDefinitionFromTemplate inherit the fix.

items.title: Generic sensitive observations can still be persisted with the original secret value
items.recommendation: Make detection and redaction symmetric. Add generic value redactors for token, secret, api_key, private_key, and CLI flag assignment forms, or narrow detection to only patterns with guaranteed redaction. After redaction, re-run validation or assert that detected sensitive values no longer remain before writing to the store.
items.reproduction: Emit an enabled `action_executed` observation with `details.command` set to `deploy --token=my-secret-value`. `validateNoSensitiveData` flags it via the contract-level token/secret detector, but `redactSensitiveFields` does not replace the value, so a spy store receives the original secret.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included redaction regression test covers `--password=secret123hunter`, which is handled by the password regex. It does not cover generic token, secret, or api_key forms that are detected by `containsSensitiveData` but not necessarily redacted by `SENSITIVE_PATTERNS`.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add `KindlingService.emit` store-boundary tests for commands such as `deploy --token=my-secret-value`, `curl ?api_key=plain-secret`, and `secret=abc123`, asserting the original values are absent from the persisted observation whenever sensitive data is detected.
items.minimumFixScope: Update `packages/kindling-integration/src/sensitive-data-validator.ts` redaction patterns and add focused regression coverage in `packages/kindling-integration/src/kindling-service.redaction.test.ts`.

items.title: Warning result consistency check ignores most summary fields
items.recommendation: Validate every derived summary field against recomputed values: byCategory, all severity keys, suppressed, and blocking. Also reject missing or extra summary counts if the contract requires exact summaries.
items.reproduction: Build a WarningResult with one unsuppressed error warning, summary.total = 1, summary.bySeverity = {}, summary.suppressed = 99, and summary.blocking = 0; validateWarningResultConsistency returns true because it only checks total and iterates over the empty bySeverity object.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked warning.schema tests cover validateWarningResultConsistency or intentionally inconsistent summary fields.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add tests that mutate each summary field from createWarningResult output and assert validateWarningResultConsistency returns false for byCategory, bySeverity, suppressed, and blocking drift.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/contracts/src/schemas/warning.schema.ts plus a focused warning schema test file or an existing contracts schema test suite.

items.title: Targeting rules can reference variants that do not exist
items.recommendation: In FeatureFlagDefinitionSchema.check, derive the declared variant key set once and reject each targeting rule whose variant is not present in variants.
items.reproduction: Parse a validFlag() with targeting containing { conditions: [{ attribute: "environment", operator: "equals", value: "prod" }], variant: "nonexistent" }; FeatureFlagDefinitionSchema.safeParse currently succeeds.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The targeting tests assert valid rules are accepted, empty rule fields are rejected, and operator value shapes are enforced, but they never supply a targeting rule whose variant is absent from the flag variants.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a FeatureFlagDefinitionSchema targeting test that passes variant: "nonexistent" and expects safeParse(...).success to be false with an error path under targeting.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/contracts/src/schemas/feature-flags.schema.ts plus the feature-flags schema test file.

items.title: Percentage targeting accepts out-of-range rollout values
items.recommendation: Constrain percentage values to a finite 0-100 range, either by using a dedicated percentage value schema or by adding range checks in the existing .check block.
items.reproduction: TargetingConditionSchema.safeParse({ attribute: "rollout", operator: "percentage", value: 250 }) currently satisfies the operator-specific check because the value is a number.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Existing tests cover a valid percentage value and reject a string value, but they do not cover boundary values below 0 or above 100.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add TargetingConditionSchema tests rejecting percentage values -1 and 101, and accepting boundary values 0 and 100 if those are intended to be inclusive.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/contracts/src/schemas/feature-flags.schema.ts plus targeted percentage operator tests.

items.title: Public pool initialisation is not regression-tested against the configured thread count
items.recommendation: Add a process-isolated integration test or helper binary that calls init_global before any rayon use, then asserts rayon::current_num_threads() equals cap_threads(num_cpus::get()). Keep the existing unit tests for idempotency and pure policy coverage.

items.title: Duplicate module IDs are silently overwritten when recursive=false
items.recommendation: Move the duplicate-ID check so it runs before both recursive and non-recursive insertions, or add the same modules.has guard in the recursive=false branch.
items.reproduction: Load an index that declares the same module heading twice with loadPlan(path, { recursive: false }). The returned plan keeps only the later module entry for that ID.

items.title: Root leaf plans with "Modules..." H2 are still misclassified as indexes
items.recommendation: Use the same real-index probe for the root file before choosing loadMultiModulePlan, or narrow detectIndexFile so only the canonical index Modules section qualifies. Preserve malformed real-index errors instead of broadly swallowing them.
items.reproduction: Call loadPlan on a single-file APS leaf document whose content includes an H2 heading like "## Modules impacted" before its tasks. The root-level detectIndexFile result is true, so loadPlan routes to loadMultiModulePlan instead of loadSingleFilePlan.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing false-positive test covers a leaf file referenced by an index, so it exercises the nested guard. It does not call loadPlan directly on a single-file leaf with the misleading heading.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a fixture for a root single-file plan containing "## Modules impacted" and assert loadPlan returns isMultiModule=false with the expected tasks loaded.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/aps/src/loader/index.ts root index detection and packages/aps/src/loader/loader.test.ts coverage for root false-positive detection.

items.title: Index templates emit legacy module statuses
items.recommendation: Change the generated index templates to use a canonical initial status such as `Proposed`, and update the tests to assert the emitted status value rather than only the presence of the `**Status:**` field.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing tests only assert that a status field exists in the generated index template; they do not assert that the status value is canonical or validate the generated template against the APS status schema.

items.title: Package version and CLI version disagree
items.recommendation: Source the CLI version from package metadata at build/runtime, or update the hard-coded CLI version as part of the package release process.
items.reproduction: Build or run the CLI and execute `anvil-codemod --version`; it reports 0.0.1 while the package metadata says 0.3.0-beta.

items.title: Sensitive observations can still be persisted unredacted on detector-only and adapter paths
items.recommendation: Make detection and redaction share one enforceable contract: either redact every issue that validateNoSensitiveData can report or fail closed when a detected issue has no redaction rule. Route AnvilKindlingAdapter.emit through the same redaction/validation logic before appendObservation, and set redacted based on whether content was changed.
items.reproduction: Emit an action_executed observation with details.command = 'ssh -i ~/.ssh/private_key user@host'. containsSensitiveData reports sensitive data, but redactSensitiveFields does not alter that value, so KindlingService.emit passes the original command to the store. Calling AnvilKindlingAdapter.emit with the same observation sends JSON.stringify(observation) to appendObservation with redacted: false.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: malicious-ai.test.ts checks that private_key and token-like payloads are detected, but it does not assert the store receives a redacted copy for those cases. kindling-service.redaction.test.ts only covers a password= command on the local KindlingService path, and there is no adapter redaction test.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a store-boundary test that emits commands containing ~/.ssh/private_key and a generic 'token sk-live-...' error message, then asserts the spy store never receives those original substrings. Add an AnvilKindlingAdapter.emit test with a fake appendObservation service that asserts content is redacted and redacted is true when sensitive data was present.
items.minimumFixScope: Update sensitive-data-validator.ts and adapter.ts, with focused tests in kindling-service.redaction.test.ts or a new adapter redaction test.

items.title: Query response validation accepts result_count values that do not match returned observations
items.recommendation: Add a QueryResponseSchema superRefine check requiring metadata.result_count === observations.length, unless the contract intentionally means total available records. If total available is required, add a separate field such as total_count and update the tests and metadata descriptions accordingly.
items.reproduction: validateQueryResponse({ metadata: { query_id, executed_at, contract_version: '1.0.0', result_count: 1000, truncated: true, truncation_reason: 'max_results' }, observations: [] }) succeeds even though zero observations are returned.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The current truncation tests intentionally construct inconsistent responses and only assert that truncation fields validate, so they encode the mismatch instead of catching it.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add validateQueryResponse tests that reject mismatched result_count and accept the same response after result_count is corrected to observations.length.
items.minimumFixScope: Update query-contract.ts validation and the malicious-ai.test.ts truncation response fixtures.

items.title: EngineEvent can represent mismatched event type and payload
items.recommendation: Make the event kind derived from EventPayload, or provide constructors that set event_type from the payload and keep raw field construction private. If wire compatibility requires both fields, add serialization/deserialization validation that rejects mismatches.
items.reproduction: Construct an EngineEvent with event_type: EventType::Error and payload: EventPayload::Progress { phase: "init".into(), current: 0, total: 1 }; this uses the same public struct-literal pattern as the included tests and has no type-level guard shown by those tests.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Existing tests cover valid matching combinations and round trips, but they never attempt to construct or deserialize a mismatched event_type/payload pair.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that attempts to deserialize an EngineEvent JSON object whose event_type does not match the EventPayload variant and asserts that deserialization fails, or add compile-time constructor tests if the fields are made private.
items.minimumFixScope: EngineEvent API and serde validation, plus tests in crates/anvil-kernel-types/tests/type_invariants.rs covering mismatched event_type/payload pairs.

items.title: Concurrent file-cache writers can lose index entries
items.recommendation: Serialize index updates with a lock file, or reload and merge the latest index immediately before saving while handling conflicts. Another option is to avoid a mutable central index for lookup and derive filenames directly from keys, keeping stats in a best-effort separate file.
items.reproduction: Start two `FileCacheProvider` instances on the same directory, have both load an empty index before either saves, then call `set("a", ...)` on one and `set("b", ...)` on the other. The final `index.json` can contain only one of the two keys depending on last writer wins.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The persistence test uses a second provider only after the first write is complete. There is no test with two providers performing overlapping writes to the same cache directory.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Create two providers sharing a temp cache directory, coordinate their `loadIndex`/`saveIndex` timing or run concurrent `set` calls repeatedly, then assert both keys remain retrievable and no index entry is lost.
items.minimumFixScope: `FileCacheProvider` index update strategy around `loadIndex`, `set`, `invalidate`, and `saveIndex`.

items.title: Cache key hashing is ambiguous for variable-length fields
items.recommendation: Canonicalize the full key input as structured data before hashing, for example `JSON.stringify(sortObjectKeys({ plan_hash, config_hash, workspace_root: normalised, extra }))`, or prefix each component with a length and delimiter that cannot be confused with data.
items.reproduction: Call `generateCacheKey` twice with identical `check_name`, `plan_hash`, `config_hash`, and `workspace_root`, but use `extra: { a: "bc", d: "e" }` for one call and `extra: { a: "b", cd: "e" }` for the other; the hashed byte stream is identical.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing tests check determinism, one changed scalar, and that adding a simple `branch` discriminator changes the hash. They do not test ambiguous concatenations across multiple fields or multiple `extra` entries.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test with two different `GateCacheKeyInput.extra` maps that currently concatenate to the same byte stream and assert their generated cache keys differ.
items.minimumFixScope: `generateCacheKey` serialization of base fields and `extra` discriminators.

items.title: Clear removes the persisted HMAC key while the provider keeps using the old in-memory key
items.recommendation: Preserve `.hmac-key` across `clear`, or make the key lifecycle explicit by recreating the same key file before subsequent writes. Alternatively reload a new mutable HMAC key after clearing before any `set` can write entries.
items.reproduction: Create a `FileCacheProvider`, call `clear()`, call `set("k", "v", ...)`, then create a second `FileCacheProvider` for the same workspace and call `get("k")`; the second provider creates a new HMAC key and rejects the entry written by the first provider.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The clear test only verifies that previously written entries are gone. It does not write a new entry after `clear` and then verify persistence through a fresh provider instance.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: After `clear`, write a new entry with the same provider, construct a fresh provider for the same directory, and assert the fresh provider can retrieve that entry.
items.minimumFixScope: `FileCacheProvider.clear` and HMAC key persistence/reload handling.

items.title: Unsigned cache index file paths can delete files outside the cache
items.recommendation: Do not trust `entryMeta.file` from the index. Derive the filename from the cache key during invalidation, or validate that the index filename is a basename matching the expected hash format and that `resolve(entriesDir, file)` stays under `entriesDir` before any read or unlink. Treat invalid index entries as index corruption without deleting their referenced paths.
items.reproduction: Create a cache index entry such as {"version":1,"entries":{"victim":{"file":"../../../victim.txt","created_at":0,"size_bytes":1}},"stats":{"hits":0,"misses":0}} under the cache directory, create the referenced victim file, then call `invalidate("victim")`; the provider unlinks the escaped path.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The file-cache invalidation tests only write normal cache entries through `set`, so index filenames are always generated by the provider. The HMAC tests tamper entry contents, not index metadata or path traversal values.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Write a hand-crafted `index.json` whose entry file contains `../` path traversal, call `invalidate` and `get` cleanup paths, and assert that files outside `entriesDir` remain untouched while the invalid index entry is removed or ignored.
items.minimumFixScope: `FileCacheProvider` index schema/path handling and invalidation/read path validation.

items.title: Published package omits files required by its advertised migration workflow
