items.minimumFixScope: apps/anvil-api/src/routes/auth.ts plus targeted rejection tests in apps/anvil-api/src/__tests__/auth.test.ts

items.title: Package README omits GET /admin/audit from the endpoint inventory
items.recommendation: Add `GET /api/v1/admin/audit` to the README endpoint table with Admin auth and a short description such as `List audit log entries`, and consider documenting the supported `action`, `actor`, `limit`, and `offset` query parameters near the admin endpoint notes.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked route tests assert runtime behaviour for `/admin/audit`, but they do not validate that the package README endpoint inventory stays in sync with declared routes.
items.minimumFixScope: Update `apps/anvil-api/README.md` only.

items.title: Callback can leave OAuth failures as uncaught 500s
items.recommendation: Wrap state decryption and GitHub code exchange in explicit try/catch handling. Redirect to /auth/error with a stable reason such as invalid_state or oauth_error, and clear the nonce for failed callback attempts where a flow has reached the callback.
items.reproduction: Call /auth/callback with a state value that causes decryptState to reject, or make exchangeGithubCode reject due to a network failure; the route has no catch block before Next.js handles the thrown error.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests were included for this feature, and the listed vitest configuration only defines how tests would be discovered.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add route tests that mock decryptState and exchangeGithubCode rejections and assert a 302 redirect to /auth/error plus oauth-nonce clearing.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/docs-shell/app/auth/callback/route.ts plus focused route tests

items.title: Refresh can burn a valid token when later work fails
items.recommendation: Move non-DB failure-prone work that can happen before mutation ahead of consuming the token, and make the consume-plus-replacement insert atomic. Alternatively make refresh rotation idempotently recoverable so a server-side failure after consuming the token does not get classified as token theft on retry.
items.reproduction: Mock consumeRefreshToken to resolve true, then make insertRefreshToken, findActiveScopesForUser, or signLicence throw. The request fails after consuming the old token; a retry with the same refresh token reaches the consumed-token path and revokes the family.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The tests cover successful rotation, invalid token states, validation, scope carry-forward, and consume race loss, but they do not simulate insert, scope lookup, or licence signing failures after consumeRefreshToken succeeds.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test where consumeRefreshToken resolves true and insertRefreshToken rejects, then assert the route does not leave the original token in a state where a retry is treated as theft or family revocation.
items.minimumFixScope: Update the refresh route and DB rotation primitive so refresh-token consumption and replacement are atomic or otherwise retry-safe; add a post-consume failure regression test.

items.title: Concurrent OTP requests can bypass the active-code cap
items.recommendation: Move the cap enforcement into an atomic database operation, such as a transaction with a per-user advisory lock or serializable isolation, or implement insertOtpCode so it conditionally inserts only when the active unexpired count is below MAX_ACTIVE_CODES and returns whether insertion happened. Only send the email after a successful conditional insert.
items.reproduction: Start with a user that has 2 active OTP rows. Send two POST /auth/otp/request requests concurrently. If both countActiveOtpCodes calls complete before either insertOtpCode commits, both requests insert and send a code, leaving 4 active codes despite MAX_ACTIVE_CODES being 3.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The current request tests mock one request at a time and assert behaviour for activeCount values of 2 and 3. They do not simulate interleaving concurrent requests or require insertOtpCode to enforce the cap atomically.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a route or query-level test that simulates two concurrent OTP requests both seeing activeCount=2 and asserts only one code is inserted/sent, preferably by testing a new atomic query helper rather than relying only on route mocks.
items.minimumFixScope: Change the OTP request persistence path so active-code cap checking and insertion are atomic, then update POST /auth/otp/request to send email only when that atomic insert succeeds.

items.title: Health requires a public licence key that the API README does not document
items.recommendation: Add `LICENSE_PUBLIC_KEY` as a required ES256 public key/SPKI PEM environment variable in `apps/anvil-api/README.md`, and mention that `/api/v1/health` validates both signing and verifying keys.
items.reproduction: Configure the API with the README-listed required variables including `LICENSE_SIGNING_KEY`, but omit `LICENSE_PUBLIC_KEY`; `GET /api/v1/health` reports `verifyingKey: "unavailable"` and returns 503.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked tests set signing and public keys only inside specific auth route suites and do not validate the README environment inventory against the health route's dependency checks.
items.minimumFixScope: Update `apps/anvil-api/README.md` environment-variable documentation for the public verification key.

items.title: Health check can be throttled by the global rate limiter
items.recommendation: Exempt `/health` from the global limiter or register the health route before `app.use('*', rateLimiter())`. Keep any desired trace/log middleware, but ensure the health handler itself is not preempted by quota state.
items.reproduction: With the API app running and valid health dependencies, issue more than 60 `GET /api/v1/health` requests within one minute from the same IP or without `x-forwarded-for`; subsequent requests return 429 from the limiter before the health handler runs.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked tests exercise auth and admin subrouters directly, and the only `index.ts` import found is for CORS preflight. There is no direct `/api/v1/health` test and no repeated health-probe test that would cross the default limiter threshold.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add an `index.ts` integration test that sends 61 `GET /api/v1/health` requests with mocked healthy DB/key dependencies and asserts the route never returns 429.
items.minimumFixScope: Change `apps/anvil-api/src/index.ts` middleware ordering or route matching so `GET /health` bypasses `rateLimiter()`.

items.title: README endpoint table omits the email-update admin route
items.recommendation: Add POST /api/v1/admin/user/email-update to the README endpoint table with an admin-auth description, and consider a short note that it rewrites beta_users.email only.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The tests exercise route behaviour, not README endpoint inventory completeness.
items.minimumFixScope: Update apps/anvil-api/README.md endpoint inventory for this route.

items.title: No-row update still writes a successful email-updated audit row
items.recommendation: Gate the audit write on the update returning a row. For example, use a single CTE statement that updates beta_users and inserts audit_log from the updated CTE, or otherwise make the audit INSERT conditional on the updated row inside the same transaction.
items.reproduction: Have findUserByEmail return an existing user, then delete that beta_users row before the transaction executes. The UPDATE returns zero rows, the audit INSERT still runs, and the endpoint returns 404 after persisting user.email.updated metadata.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing race test explicitly mocks the problematic transaction result with an audit row present and only asserts the 404 response; it does not assert that a success audit is avoided.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test for the deleted-during-update path that verifies no user.email.updated audit row can be written when the UPDATE returns no row, ideally via the helper or SQL fragment that implements the conditional audit.
items.minimumFixScope: Change the email-update transaction SQL so audit logging is dependent on the UPDATE result, then tighten the deleted-during-update test around that invariant.

items.title: Email updates can make an already-approved signup look pending again
items.recommendation: Make the approval relationship stable before shipping this route. Either update the waitlist approval model to use a stable user id or approved marker, or have this endpoint update enough waitlist state that old approved signups cannot re-enter pending/batch approval queues while still preserving historical signup evidence elsewhere.
items.reproduction: Seed a waitlist row for old@example.com and an approved beta_users row for old@example.com. Call POST /admin/user/email-update with newEmail=new@example.com. Then list pending waitlist entries or run POST /admin/approve with batch mode; the old waitlist row is eligible because approval is email-derived and the beta_users email no longer matches it.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The email-update tests assert the route response and direct error cases only; they do not exercise GET /admin/waitlist or POST /admin/approve batch behaviour after an email rewrite.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that performs an email update for an approved waitlist user, then verifies the old waitlist address is not returned as pending and is not selected by batch approval.
items.minimumFixScope: Adjust the email-update flow plus the waitlist approval derivation or waitlist persistence model so approved status is not keyed solely by the mutable beta_users.email value.

items.title: Confirmed device code is deleted before downstream token issuance can fail
items.recommendation: Move the irreversible consume and refresh-token persistence into one atomic database operation, or otherwise ensure the device code is only consumed after all fallible preconditions needed for a successful response have completed. A robust shape is: validate user and sign the licence first, then atomically DELETE the confirmed unexpired code and INSERT the refresh token in the same transaction/statement, returning success only if both DB mutations commit.
items.reproduction: In the /poll test setup, mock pollDeviceCode to return a confirmed unexpired row, consumeDeviceCode to return { user_id: 'user-1' }, findUserById to return an active user, and insertRefreshToken to reject. The first request fails after consumeDeviceCode has run; a retry with consumeDeviceCode returning null produces { status: 'expired' }.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The current tests cover already-expired rows, already-consumed rows, suspended users, and the happy path, but they do not simulate failures after consumeDeviceCode succeeds and before the confirmed response is returned.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a /poll test where insertRefreshToken rejects after consumeDeviceCode succeeds, and assert the implementation does not leave the code consumed without issuing credentials. If the fix uses an atomic helper, assert that helper is called once and that separate consume-before-insert behavior is gone.
items.minimumFixScope: Change the confirmed branch of POST /auth/device/poll and its DB helper contract so consumption and refresh-token insertion are atomic with respect to downstream failure; add a targeted regression test in apps/anvil-api/src/__tests__/auth-device.test.ts.

items.title: Footer year is cached for the lifetime of the server module
items.recommendation: Move the year calculation into `HomePage` so it is evaluated for each dynamic render, or remove `force-dynamic` and intentionally accept a build-time/static year with a documented regeneration strategy.
items.reproduction: Start the docs-shell server before midnight on December 31, keep the same process running past January 1, then request `/`; the footer can still show the prior year because `COPYRIGHT_YEAR` was initialised when the module was loaded.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests were provided for this route, and there is no time-bound rendering test that controls the system date or simulates a long-running module instance across a year boundary.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a route/component rendering test that imports the page once, renders it with a mocked current date, advances the mocked date to the next year without re-importing the module, and verifies the footer uses the new year after the fix.
items.minimumFixScope: Change `apps/docs-shell/app/page.tsx` so the year is computed inside `HomePage`, then add a focused test for the footer year behavior if the app's test setup supports rendering React server components.

items.title: Login redirect URI is derived from the incoming request origin
items.recommendation: Build the callback URL from an explicit trusted configuration value such as DOCS_PUBLIC_ORIGIN or DOCS_CALLBACK_URL, validate it at startup/request time, and use the request only for the user-controlled next parameter after validateNext.
items.reproduction: Send GET /auth/login with an unexpected Host header, for example Host: internal.example, and inspect the Location header. The GitHub authorize URL will contain redirect_uri=https://internal.example/auth/callback instead of the intended public callback origin.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests are linked for this route, and the current context has no assertion for redirect_uri construction under alternate request origins.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a route test that calls GET with a forged or non-public request origin and asserts the GitHub Location header uses the configured public callback URL, not the request origin.
items.minimumFixScope: Update apps/docs-shell/app/auth/login/route.ts to source redirect_uri from trusted configuration and add a focused route test for the authorize redirect URL.

items.title: Test files with .tsx/.mts/.cts extensions do not receive the test rule relaxations
items.recommendation: Expand the test override globs to cover every TypeScript extension supported by the main block, for example **/*.{test,spec}.{ts,tsx,mts,cts}, and include config files only where needed.
items.reproduction: Create packages/example/src/component.test.tsx containing console.log('x') and an explicit any annotation, then lint with this shared config. It will match the broad TypeScript block but not the test override.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature lists no linked tests, and there is no included test exercising glob coverage for the exported config.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a package-level test that loads typescriptConfig and asserts .test.tsx, .spec.tsx, .test.mts, and .test.cts paths match the relaxed test rule override.
items.minimumFixScope: Update packages/tooling/eslint-config/typescript.mjs test override globs and add focused config-shape coverage.

items.title: Blank URL or actor values bypass defaults
items.recommendation: Normalize configuration inputs before precedence decisions. Treat empty or whitespace-only URL and actor env values as absent so defaults/fallbacks apply, and either reject blank flag values explicitly or normalize them consistently. Keep blank keys rejected as missing.
items.reproduction: resolveConfig({}, { env: { ANVIL_ADMIN_KEY: 'k', ANVIL_ADMIN_URL: '', ANVIL_ADMIN_ACTOR: '' }, getGitEmail: () => 'git@example.com', getOsUser: () => 'osuser' }) returns { url: '', key: 'k', actor: '' } instead of defaulting or rejecting the blank values.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The config tests cover omitted URL/actor values and omitted keys, but they do not exercise empty-string or whitespace-only values from env or flags.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add resolveConfig tests where ANVIL_ADMIN_URL and ANVIL_ADMIN_ACTOR are empty or whitespace-only while key is present; assert URL defaults to DEFAULT_URL and actor falls through to git email or OS user, or assert a deliberate validation error if blank flags should be invalid.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/admin-cli/src/config.ts input normalization plus focused tests in apps/admin-cli/src/__tests__/config.test.ts

items.title: Refresh token consumption is not guarded against concurrent revocation or expiry
items.recommendation: Include the validity predicates in the UPDATE, for example WHERE id = $id AND consumed_at IS NULL AND revoked_at IS NULL AND expires_at > now(). If callers need to distinguish concurrent reuse from concurrent revocation/expiry, return a more specific result shape or re-read after a false update.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The provided queries.test file only covers findActiveScopesForUser and revokeRefreshFamilyAndAccessTokensForUser. Refresh-route tests in the repo mock consumeRefreshToken, so they cannot verify the SQL predicate used by the real helper.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a query-level test for consumeRefreshToken asserting the emitted SQL includes consumed_at IS NULL, revoked_at IS NULL, and expires_at > now(), or exercise it against a test database with a token revoked between lookup and consume.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/anvil-api/src/db/queries.ts consumeRefreshToken plus a focused query regression test.

items.title: Audit read queries drop the auth_method written by audit inserts
items.recommendation: Select auth_method in findAuditEntries and findRecentAuditForEmail, and keep the optional parser only if legacy rows or fixtures still need it.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The provided queries.test file does not exercise audit reads. Existing route-level audit tests use mocked findAuditEntries/findRecentAuditForEmail responses and do not assert auth_method round-trips from the database helpers.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a queries.test case that feeds an audit row with auth_method: 'per_operator' through findAuditEntries/findRecentAuditForEmail and asserts the returned item includes that value.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/anvil-api/src/db/queries.ts audit SELECT lists plus focused query tests.

items.title: getAll allows config keys to change the returned object's prototype
items.recommendation: Build getAll results with a null-prototype object, for example const result = Object.create(null) as Record<string, unknown>, or explicitly reject reserved prototype keys such as __proto__, prototype, and constructor before storing or exporting config.
items.reproduction: const loader = new ConfigLoader(); loader.set('__proto__', { admin: true }); const all = loader.getAll(); all.admin === true while Object.hasOwn(all, '__proto__') === false.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: packages/anvil/core/src/config/config.test.ts only verifies ordinary keys like a, b, zero, empty, nul, and undef; it does not exercise prototype-sensitive keys or assert own-property behaviour for getAll().
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a ConfigLoader getAll test that sets '__proto__' to an object, asserts the returned object does not inherit that object's properties, and asserts Object.hasOwn(result, '__proto__') or that the key is rejected according to the chosen fix.
items.minimumFixScope: Change ConfigLoader.getAll to use a null-prototype result object and add the reserved-key regression test in packages/anvil/core/src/config/config.test.ts.

items.title: Application preset inherits composite mode while disabling declarations
items.recommendation: Override composite to false in app.json, or split composite into a separate build/reference preset that app.json does not inherit. Keep the README description aligned with the chosen contract.
items.reproduction: Create a tsconfig.json extending @eddacraft/anvil-tsconfig/app.json with any included src file and run tsc --noEmit false; TypeScript rejects the inherited composite/declaration:false combination.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests were included for this package, and there is no fixture that typechecks each exported preset through TypeScript.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a small fixture or script that runs tsc --showConfig or tsc -p against each exported preset, including app.json, and asserts the advertised presets compile.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/tooling/tsconfig/app.json plus any README wording if the app preset contract changes.

items.title: Node type preset does not declare its required type package
items.recommendation: Declare @types/node as a peerDependency with a matching devDependency for local validation, or remove forced node types from presets that do not require Node globals and document the consumer requirement explicitly.
items.reproduction: In a package that installs only @eddacraft/anvil-tsconfig and typescript, extend base.json, node.json, or react.json and run tsc; TypeScript attempts to resolve the node type library from the consumer project and can fail when @types/node is absent.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No package tests were included, and there is no isolated consumer install/typecheck fixture that validates the published package metadata includes all ambient type requirements.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add an isolated fixture or package smoke test that installs/builds against the packed @eddacraft/anvil-tsconfig package and verifies every exported preset resolves its configured types.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/tooling/tsconfig/package.json, with possible preset or README updates if the node types contract is narrowed.

items.title: database_path accepts paths outside the project root
items.recommendation: Validate database_path at the config boundary: reject empty strings, absolute paths, URL/protocol-like paths, and any path segment that escapes the project root after normalisation/resolution. Prefer returning a normalised project-relative path or a resolved path that has been checked to remain under projectRoot.
items.reproduction: KindlingConfigSchema.safeParse({ enabled: true, database_path: '../../outside.db' }) succeeds even though the field contract says the path is relative to the project root.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests only parse enabled/disabled configs for service redaction setup and exercise query/observation contracts; none assert database_path validation or loadKindlingConfig filesystem-boundary behaviour.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add config tests that reject database_path values like '', '/tmp/kindling.db', '../kindling.db', '../../outside.db', and 'C:\\temp\\kindling.db', while accepting '.anvil/kindling.db' and nested project-relative paths.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/kindling-integration/src/config.ts schema/loading validation plus targeted config tests

items.title: Package test script starts Vitest in watch mode outside CI
items.recommendation: Change the script to `vitest run`, and add a separate watch script such as `test:watch` if interactive watch mode is useful.

items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a package-script smoke check that runs `pnpm --filter @eddacraft/anvil-api test -- --run` or the final `test` script in a non-watch environment and fails if it does not exit successfully.
items.minimumFixScope: Update `apps/anvil-api/package.json` so the `test` script uses Vitest run mode.

items.title: Suppression test does not assert which finding is suppressed
items.recommendation: Assert the suppressed finding identity, not just the count and reason. At minimum check `suppressed[0].key == "AWS_ROTATED_KEY"` and `suppressed[0].finding.pattern_name == "AWS Key"`, and assert the other fixture findings are not suppressed.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The current assertions cover aggregate counts and reason text only; they never bind the suppression metadata to the rotated AWS fixture line.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Strengthen `aws_key_fixture_yields_structured_findings` to locate findings by key and assert `AWS_ROTATED_KEY` is suppressed with the expected reason while `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` and `GITHUB_TOKEN` are unsuppressed.
items.minimumFixScope: Update assertions in `crates/anvil-checks/tests/surfenv_env_scan.rs` only.

items.title: Package test script does not declare its runner dependency
items.recommendation: Declare `vitest` in `packages/libs/render/package.json` devDependencies, or route the package test script through an explicitly supported workspace-level test command if package-local execution is not intended.
items.reproduction: From a clean install scoped to `packages/libs/render`, run `pnpm test`; the script will fail if `vitest` is not provided by an ancestor workspace dependency.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests or package-script validation were included for this feature, and the package manifest itself does not assert that `vitest` is available locally.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a manifest/tooling check that each package script invoking a binary has that binary declared locally or is explicitly allowlisted as workspace-provided.
items.minimumFixScope: Update the render package manifest or central package-script policy so the `test` script has an explicit, documented runner dependency.

items.title: Fixture assertion can pass after losing one of the intended findings
items.recommendation: Assert the exact expected finding set, for example by comparing sorted tuples of (key, indicator, suppressed) against DATABASE_URL/ProdHostSegment/false, FEATURE_FLAGS_ENV/ValueMentionsProduction/false, SECRET_PROD/KeySuffixProd/false, and LEGACY_HOST/ProdHostSegment/true.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The current owned test checks only aggregate cardinality plus two specific keys; it never validates the complete fixture output or the indicators for the prod-db and production-value cases.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Update prod_in_local_fixture_yields_expected_findings to build the exact expected tuple set from findings and assert equality, including both unsuppressed DATABASE_URL and FEATURE_FLAGS_ENV entries.
items.minimumFixScope: Tighten assertions in crates/anvil-checks/tests/surfenv_prod_value.rs; no production code change is required.

items.title: Filtered-file test can consume the wrong debounce batch
items.recommendation: Keep the filtered and accepted writes inside the same debounce window, or drain/loop until a batch containing index.ts is observed while asserting that no observed batch includes README.md. Avoid assuming the first received batch is the accepted-file batch when the test deliberately waits longer than the debounce interval between writes.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: This file is the integration test itself, and the scenario under review contains the timing assumption. There is no included test that exercises a filtered-only event followed by an accepted event after a debounce flush without requiring the accepted event to appear in the first received batch.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a watcher test that creates a filtered file, waits longer than the debounce window, then creates an accepted file and reads batches until the accepted file is seen, asserting filtered paths never appear in any received batch.
items.minimumFixScope: Update crates/anvil-kernel/tests/watcher_integration.rs so filters_out_non_parseable_files no longer assumes the first received batch after two timing-separated writes is the batch containing index.ts.

items.title: Schema version compatibility is only asserted on self-produced payloads
items.recommendation: Add negative deserialisation cases for invalid schema_version values, especially an unknown major such as anvil.protection-claim.v2 and a missing schema_version if the field is required. If the intended API contract is to ignore schema_version and validate elsewhere, document that boundary in the test comments so future maintainers do not mistake this suite for full envelope compatibility coverage.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Current tests only compare schema_version after serialising known-good ProtectionClaim values or deserialise fixtures that already contain the expected v1 string; no test exercises an invalid or absent schema_version.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test like `unknown_schema_version_rejects_at_contract_boundary` with a valid `worktree_state` and `surfaces` array but `schema_version: "anvil.protection-claim.v2"`, plus a missing-schema fixture if required by the contract.
items.minimumFixScope: Update `crates/anvil-cli/tests/protection_claim_states.rs` with explicit schema_version compatibility fixtures, or narrow the suite documentation to state that schema-version gating is enforced outside this contract test.

items.title: Unix cfg runs the test on unsupported Unix targets
items.recommendation: Narrow the crate-level gate to the supported daemon credential platforms, for example `#![cfg(any(target_os = "linux", target_os = "macos"))]`, or split compile-only Unix coverage from the live-daemon E2E.
items.reproduction: Run this integration test on a Unix target other than Linux or macOS; the file is included by `#![cfg(unix)]` even though its own documented daemon credential dependency is unsupported there.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The tests are the gated artifact; they only exercise the happy path on targets where the binary is built, and there is no target-cfg check proving unsupported Unix platforms are excluded.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a compile/cfg assertion or CI metadata check that this integration test is enabled only for Linux/macOS unless peer credential support is added for another Unix target.
items.minimumFixScope: Update the file-level cfg and the adjacent comment to match the actual supported target set.

items.title: Temporary test directories leak whenever a file-backed test panics
items.recommendation: Replace the PathBuf helper with an RAII temporary directory guard such as tempfile::TempDir, or return a small guard type that removes the directory in Drop. Make directory creation fail loudly with expect so setup failures point at the helper.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The tests only exercise successful completion paths; the cleanup calls are after assertions, so no existing test can prove cleanup happens when a test fails before reaching remove_dir_all.
items.minimumFixScope: Update temp_dir and the six file-backed tests in crates/anvil-checks/tests/antipattern_scanning.rs to hold an RAII temp directory for the duration of each test.

items.title: Package test script defaults to Vitest watch mode outside CI
items.recommendation: Change the package script to `vitest run` and add a separate `test:watch` script if interactive watch mode is desired.
items.reproduction: Run `pnpm --filter @eddacraft/anvil-edda-stack test` from an interactive non-CI shell; the command enters Vitest watch mode instead of exiting after one run.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests validate package script semantics, and the existing Vitest tests exercise source behaviour only after the runner has started.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a package metadata check that asserts package `test` scripts use non-watch commands such as `vitest run`, with watch mode exposed through `test:watch`.
items.minimumFixScope: Update `packages/edda-stack/package.json` scripts only.

items.title: Native test freshness guard ignores Rust dependency inputs
items.recommendation: Extend scripts/check-binding-fresh.mjs to consider every compile input that can affect the .node artifact: at minimum crates/anvil-checks-napi/Cargo.toml, build.rs, Cargo.lock if applicable, and the relevant path dependency source trees. Alternatively replace the mtime heuristic with a small build stamp emitted after napi build that records the inputs or commit hash used for the artifact.
items.reproduction: Build the binding once, then modify or touch a source file under crates/anvil-checks/src or update crates/anvil-checks-napi/Cargo.toml without rebuilding. Run pnpm --filter @eddacraft/anvil-checks-native test; the pretest check only looks at crates/anvil-checks-napi/src and can allow the stale .node to load.

items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a node:test or shell-level test for scripts/check-binding-fresh.mjs that creates a temporary package layout with a .node file newer than local src but older than a mocked path dependency file, then asserts the guard exits non-zero.
items.minimumFixScope: Update the freshness guard and add targeted coverage for dependency-input staleness; the package.json test command can remain unchanged.

items.title: Package test script may enter Vitest watch mode outside CI
items.recommendation: Change the package script to `vitest run` for deterministic package-script behavior. Add a separate watch script such as `test:watch` if interactive watch mode is desired.

items.title: Windows-negative test still relies on home isolation the file marks unreliable

items.title: Timeout budget is not exercised on a hanging probe target

items.title: Filter tests can pass when allowed files are filtered out
items.recommendation: Assert the exact expected surviving count for the filtered initial scans, e.g. require a snapshot with files_watched == 1. Add a runtime positive-control test that runs with exclude_patterns = ["vendor/**"], writes an included src/**/*.ts file that would emit a violation, and asserts that violation is received.

items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add included_runtime_change_still_emits_violation_with_exclude_config using exclude_patterns vec!["vendor/**"], then write src/app/added.ts importing a new external package and assert a violation path containing src/app/added.

items.title: Sleep-based watcher coordination makes the integration tests race-prone
items.recommendation: Replace fixed sleeps with deadline-based polling on receiver events. Wait for the initial snapshot before draining and writing runtime files, then wait until the expected violation or a clear timeout is observed. Use the same pattern for initial-scan count assertions instead of collecting after a fixed 400 ms.
items.reproduction: Run the test binary under CPU or I/O contention so the initial scan takes longer than 300 ms or notify delivery exceeds the fixed collection window; the runtime control can fail even though the implementation is correct.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: These tests are the coverage in question; their timing strategy is not validated by another deterministic synchronization point.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Refactor the tests around helper functions like wait_for_snapshot_files(rx, expected, timeout) and wait_for_violation_path(rx, predicate, timeout), then use them in both runtime tests.
items.minimumFixScope: Update crates/anvil-kernel/tests/watch_pattern_filter.rs to poll for semantic events with deadlines instead of sleeping and try_iter-draining.

items.title: Concurrency test does not assert that every writer's record is preserved

items.title: Fresh-engine loop does not exercise residual engine state determinism

items.title: Idempotency test passes even when status verification fails

items.title: Verbose JSON auth test can pass with stdout leakage

items.title: Update mode can race round-trip readers against fixture writers
items.recommendation: Make update mode self-contained for every test that reads fixtures. For example, have `every_fixture_round_trips_through_protection_claim` generate/update the expected fixtures before reading when ANVIL_UPDATE_FIXTURES is set, or skip the round-trip reader in update mode after the producer/layout test has refreshed fixtures. The normal status_render run also passes because all current fixtures are already present, so it does not exercise the missing-fixture update path.

items.title: Advertised edda list filters are not covered by the integration suite
items.recommendation: Add integration tests that invoke --status with a non-default status, --confidence with mixed confidence values, and --since with memories on both sides of the boundary. Keep the fixtures in the existing index/full-memory shape so the tests remain representative of the MemoryStore layout.

items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add tests such as edda_list_json_filters_by_status, edda_list_json_filters_by_confidence, and edda_list_json_filters_by_since that each create mixed fixture entries and assert both total and returned IDs.

items.title: Dual-engine comparison ignores duplicate violation counts

items.title: ports test script can pass without exercising any tests
items.recommendation: Add at least one meaningful ports package test, or make this package test target fail when no tests are discovered by removing or overriding pass-with-no-tests behaviour.

items.title: Smuggled non-object findings test does not isolate the smuggling case
items.recommendation: Use a valid finding object mixed with a non-object element, then assert the command fails specifically because findings arrays cannot contain non-object entries.

items.minimumFixScope: Adjust the smuggled non-object fixture and expected error assertion in this integration test.

items.title: Oversized input test would still pass if the size guard were removed
items.recommendation: Make the oversized fixture syntactically valid JSON while still exceeding the cap, and assert the error identifies the input-size limit rather than generic parse failure.

items.title: Stdio suite advertises anvil_apply_patch without exercising its call path
items.recommendation: Add stdio-level tests that call anvil_apply_patch against a temp workspace, assert the patch is applied and the MCP payload is valid, and add an out-of-root workspace rejection case that proves a sibling file remains unchanged.

items.title: Secret-like fixtures are still committed as contiguous literals
items.recommendation: Build all realistic secret fixtures from non-contiguous parts at runtime, as the path-normalisation test already does, or centralise fixture construction in helpers that deliberately avoid storing full secret shapes in source.

items.title: Repeated install test only checks pre-commit idempotence
items.recommendation: Assert `hook.pre-push.command` has exactly one expected value after repeated `install --config`, matching the pre-commit idempotence assertion.

items.title: Config assertions read inherited global/system Git hook settings
items.recommendation: Make `config_get_all` query only repository-local config, for example `git -C <dir> config --local --get-all <key>`. Also consider setting `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1` and temp `HOME`/`XDG_CONFIG_HOME` for all Git inspection commands if the test must exercise default lookup behaviour elsewhere.

items.minimumFixScope: Update the test helper and any related Git inspection commands in `crates/anvil-cli/tests/hooks_config_mode.rs` to read local repo config only or fully isolate Git's config environment.

items.title: Busy-response fixture does not enforce JSON-RPC id echo
items.recommendation: Make the busy assertion validate the expected id, either by changing it to `assert_busy_response(response, expected_idx)` / `assert_busy_response(response, expected_id)` or by adding a dedicated assertion for the public `busy_request(idx)` pair.

items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The local Rust test checks the id separately after calling the helper, so it covers only this implementation path. No test proves the reusable helper rejects a wrong-id busy response.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a unit test that invokes `assert_busy_response` with a wrong id and expects a panic, once the helper accepts the expected id.
items.minimumFixScope: Update `assert_busy_response` and its callers to include expected-id validation.

items.title: Reusable contract API is trapped inside a Rust integration-test crate

items.recommendation: Make update mode deterministic: either have a single test own fixture regeneration before all reads, make `every_fixture_round_trips_through_protection_claim` generate/read the expected bytes in-memory when update mode is set, or document/use `-- --test-threads=1` and order-independent setup that writes all fixtures before assertions.

If `every_fixture_round_trips_through_protection_claim` runs first, it panics on the missing fixture instead of regenerating.
